<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service">InfluxDB OSS API Service v2.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

The InfluxDB v2 API provides a programmatic interface for all interactions with InfluxDB. Access the InfluxDB API using the `/api/v2/` endpoint.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api/v2">https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api/v2</a>

License: <a href="https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT">MIT</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (TokenAuthentication)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header. Use the [Token authentication](#section/Authentication/TokenAuthentication)
scheme to authenticate to the InfluxDB API.

In your API requests, send an `Authorization` header.
For the header value, provide the word `Token` followed by a space and an InfluxDB API token.
The word `Token` is case-sensitive.

### Syntax

`Authorization: Token INFLUX_API_TOKEN`

### Example

#### Use Token authentication with cURL

The following example shows how to use cURL to send an API request that uses Token authentication:

```sh
curl --request GET "INFLUX_URL/api/v2/buckets" \
    --header "Authorization: Token INFLUX_API_TOKEN"
```

Replace the following:

  - *`INFLUX_URL`*: your InfluxDB URL
  - *`INFLUX_API_TOKEN`*: your [InfluxDB API token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token)

### Related endpoints

- [`/authorizations` endpoints](#tag/Authorizations-(API-tokens))

### Related guides

- [Authorize API requests](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api-guide/api_intro/#authentication)
- [Manage API tokens](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/)

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic ### Basic authentication scheme

Use the HTTP Basic authentication scheme for InfluxDB `/api/v2` API operations that support it:

### Syntax

`Authorization: Basic BASE64_ENCODED_CREDENTIALS`

To construct the `BASE64_ENCODED_CREDENTIALS`, combine the username and
the password with a colon (`USERNAME:PASSWORD`), and then encode the
resulting string in [base64](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Base64).
Many HTTP clients encode the credentials for you before sending the
request.

_**Warning**: Base64-encoding can easily be reversed to obtain the original
username and password. It is used to keep the data intact and does not provide
security. You should always use HTTPS when authenticating or sending a request with
sensitive information._

### Examples

In the examples, replace the following:

- **`USERNAME`**: InfluxDB username
- **`PASSWORD`**: InfluxDB [API token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token)
- **`INFLUX_URL`**: your InfluxDB URL

#### Encode credentials with cURL

The following example shows how to use cURL to send an API request that uses Basic authentication.
With the `--user` option, cURL encodes the credentials and passes them
in the `Authorization: Basic` header.

```sh
curl --get "INFLUX_URL/api/v2/signin"
    --user "USERNAME":"PASSWORD"
```

#### Encode credentials with Flux

The Flux [`http.basicAuth()` function](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/stdlib/http/basicauth/) returns a Base64-encoded
basic authentication header using a specified username and password combination.

#### Encode credentials with JavaScript

The following example shows how to use the JavaScript `btoa()` function
to create a Base64-encoded string:

```js
btoa('USERNAME:PASSWORD')
```

The output is the following:

```js
'VVNFUk5BTUU6UEFTU1dPUkQ='
```

Once you have the Base64-encoded credentials, you can pass them in the
`Authorization` header--for example:

```sh
curl --get "INFLUX_URL/api/v2/signin"
    --header "Authorization: Basic VVNFUk5BTUU6UEFTU1dPUkQ="
```

To learn more about HTTP authentication, see
[Mozilla Developer Network (MDN) Web Docs, HTTP authentication](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Authentication)._

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-authorizations-api-tokens">Authorizations (API tokens)</h1>

Create and manage authorizations (API tokens).

An _authorization_ contains a list of `read` and `write`
permissions for organization resources and provides an API token for authentication.
An authorization belongs to an organization and only contains permissions for that organization.

We recommend creating a generic user to create and manage tokens for writing data.

### User sessions with authorizations

Optionally, when creating an authorization, you can scope it to a specific user.
If a user signs in with username and password, creating a _user session_,
the session carries the permissions granted by all the user's authorizations.
For more information, see [how to assign a token to a specific user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/create-token/).
To create a user session, use the [`POST /api/v2/signin` endpoint](#operation/PostSignin).

### Related endpoints

- [Signin](#tag/Signin)
- [Signout](#tag/Signout)

### Related guides

- [Authorize API requests](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api-guide/api_intro/#authentication)
- [Manage API tokens](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/)
- [Assign a token to a specific user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/create-token/)


## List authorizations

<a id="opIdGetAuthorizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/authorizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /authorizations`

Lists authorizations.

To limit which authorizations are returned, pass query parameters in your request.
If no query parameters are passed, InfluxDB returns all authorizations.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- InfluxDB Cloud doesn't expose [API token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token)
  values in `GET /api/v2/authorizations` responses;
  returns `token: redacted` for all authorizations.

#### Required permissions

To retrieve an authorization, the request must use an API token that has the
following permissions:

- `read-authorizations`
- `read-user` for the user that the authorization is scoped to

#### Related guides

- [View tokens](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/view-tokens/)


<h3 id="list-authorizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|userID|query|string|false|A user ID.<br>Only returns authorizations scoped to the specified [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user).<br>|
|user|query|string|false|A user name.<br>Only returns authorizations scoped to the specified [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user).<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID. Only returns authorizations that belong to the specified [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization).|
|org|query|string|false|An organization name.<br>Only returns authorizations that belong to the specified [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization).<br>|
|token|query|string|false|An API [token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token) value.<br>Specifies an authorization by its `token` property value<br>and returns the authorization.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Doesn't support this parameter. InfluxDB OSS ignores the `token=` parameter,<br>  applies other parameters, and then returns the result.<br><br>#### Limitations<br><br>- The parameter is non-repeatable. If you specify more than one,<br>  only the first one is used. If a resource with the specified<br>  property value doesn't exist, then the response body contains an empty list.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com"
  },
  "authorizations": [
    {
      "status": "active",
      "description": "string",
      "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "orgID": "string",
      "permissions": [
        {
          "action": "read",
          "resource": {
            "type": "authorizations",
            "id": "string",
            "name": "string",
            "orgID": "string",
            "org": "string"
          }
        }
      ],
      "id": "string",
      "token": "string",
      "userID": "string",
      "user": "string",
      "org": "string",
      "links": {
        "self": "/api/v2/authorizations/1",
        "user": "/api/v2/users/12"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-authorizations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success. The response body contains a list of authorizations.<br><br>If the response body is missing authorizations that you expect, check that the API<br>token used in the request has `read-user` permission for the users (`userID` property value)<br>in those authorizations.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- **Warning**: The response body contains authorizations with their<br>  [API token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token) values in clear text.<br>- If the request uses an  _[operator token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/#operator-token)_,<br>  InfluxDB OSS returns authorizations for all organizations in the instance.<br>|[Authorizations](#schemaauthorizations)|
|400|Bad Request|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-authorizations-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **401**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|read-only|The HTTP status code description. Default is `unauthorized`.<br>|
|message|string|false|read-only|A human-readable message that may contain detail about the error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|unauthorized|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Create an authorization

<a id="opIdPostAuthorizations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/authorizations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "orgID": "INFLUX_ORG_ID",
    "description": "iot_users read buckets",
    "permissions": [
      {
        "action": "read",
        "resource": {
          "type": "buckets"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /authorizations`

Creates an authorization and returns the authorization with the
generated API [token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token).

Use this endpoint to create an authorization, which generates an API token
with permissions to `read` or `write` to a specific resource or `type` of resource.
The API token is the authorization's `token` property value.

To follow best practices for secure API token generation and retrieval,
InfluxDB enforces access restrictions on API tokens.

  - InfluxDB allows access to the API token value immediately after the authorization is created.
  - You can’t change access (read/write) permissions for an API token after it’s created.
  - Tokens stop working when the user who created the token is deleted.

We recommend the following for managing your tokens:

  - Create a generic user to create and manage tokens for writing data.
  - Store your tokens in a secure password vault for future access.

#### Required permissions

- `write-authorizations`
- `write-user` for the user that the authorization is scoped to

#### Related guides

- [Create a token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/create-token/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "orgID": "INFLUX_ORG_ID",
  "description": "iot_users read buckets",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "action": "read",
      "resource": {
        "type": "buckets"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-authorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|body|body|[AuthorizationPostRequest](#schemaauthorizationpostrequest)|true|The authorization to create.|
|» status|body|string|false|Status of the token. If `inactive`, InfluxDB rejects requests that use the token.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the token.|
|» orgID|body|string|true|An organization ID.<br>Specifies the organization that owns the authorization.<br>|
|» userID|body|string|false|A user ID.<br>Specifies the user that the authorization is scoped to.<br><br>When a user authenticates with username and password,<br>InfluxDB generates a _user session_ with all the permissions<br>specified by all the user's authorizations.<br>|
|» permissions|body|[[Permission](#schemapermission)]|true|A list of permissions for an authorization.<br>In the list, provide at least one `permission` object.<br><br>In a `permission`, the `resource.type` property grants access to all<br>resources of the specified type.<br>To grant access to only a specific resource, specify the<br>`resource.id` property.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|inactive|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "status": "active",
  "description": "string",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "orgID": "string",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "action": "read",
      "resource": {
        "type": "authorizations",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "orgID": "string",
        "org": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "token": "string",
  "userID": "string",
  "user": "string",
  "org": "string",
  "links": {
    "self": "/api/v2/authorizations/1",
    "user": "/api/v2/users/12"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-authorization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Success. The authorization is created. The response body contains the<br>authorization.<br>|[Authorization](#schemaauthorization)|
|400|Bad Request|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

|message|string|false|read-only|A human-readable message that may contain detail about the error.|

|code|unauthorized|

## Retrieve an authorization

<a id="opIdGetAuthorizationsID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/authorizations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /authorizations/{authID}`

Retrieves an authorization.

Use this endpoint to retrieve information about an API token, including
the token's permissions and the user that the token is scoped to.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- InfluxDB OSS returns
  [API token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token) values in authorizations.
- If the request uses an _[operator token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/#operator-token)_,
  InfluxDB OSS returns authorizations for all organizations in the instance.

#### Related guides

- [View tokens](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/view-tokens/)


<a href="https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/view-tokens/">View tokens</a>

<h3 id="retrieve-an-authorization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|authID|path|string|true|An authorization ID. Specifies the authorization to retrieve.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": "active",
  "description": "string",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "orgID": "string",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "action": "read",
      "resource": {
        "type": "authorizations",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "orgID": "string",
        "org": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "token": "string",
  "userID": "string",
  "user": "string",
  "org": "string",

    "self": "/api/v2/authorizations/1",
    "user": "/api/v2/users/12"

}
```


## Update an API token to be active or inactive

<a id="opIdPatchAuthorizationsID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/authorizations/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "status": "active",
    "description": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /authorizations/{authID}`

Updates an authorization.

Use this endpoint to set an API token's status to be _active_ or _inactive_.
InfluxDB rejects requests that use inactive API tokens.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "status": "active",
  "description": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-api-token-to-be-active-or-inactive-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|authID|path|string|true|An authorization ID. Specifies the authorization to update.|
|body|body|[AuthorizationUpdateRequest](#schemaauthorizationupdaterequest)|true|In the request body, provide the authorization properties to update.|
|» status|body|string|false|Status of the token. If `inactive`, InfluxDB rejects requests that use the token.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the token.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|inactive|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": "active",
  "description": "string",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "orgID": "string",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "action": "read",
      "resource": {
        "type": "authorizations",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "orgID": "string",
        "org": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "token": "string",
```

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-buckets">Buckets</h1>

Store your data in InfluxDB [buckets](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#bucket).
A bucket is a named location where time series data is stored. All buckets
have a [retention period](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#retention-period),
a duration of time that each data point persists. InfluxDB drops all
points with timestamps older than the bucket’s retention period.
A bucket belongs to an organization.

### Related guides

- [Manage buckets](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/buckets/)


## List buckets

<a id="opIdGetBuckets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/buckets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /buckets`

Lists [buckets](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#bucket).

InfluxDB retrieves buckets owned by the
[organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization)
associated with the authorization
([API token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token)).
To limit which buckets are returned, pass query parameters in your request.
If no query parameters are passed, InfluxDB returns all buckets up to the
default `limit`.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- If you use an _[operator token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/#operator-token)_
  to authenticate your request, InfluxDB retrieves resources for _all
  organizations_ in the instance.
  To retrieve resources for only a specific organization, use the
  `org` parameter or the `orgID` parameter to specify the organization.

#### Required permissions

| Action                    | Permission required |
|:--------------------------|:--------------------|
| Retrieve _user buckets_   | `read-buckets`      |
| Retrieve [_system buckets_](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/internals/system-buckets/) | `read-orgs`         |

#### Related Guides

- [Manage buckets](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/buckets/)


<h3 id="list-buckets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|offset|query|integer|false|The offset for pagination.<br>The number of records to skip.<br><br>For more information about pagination parameters, see [Pagination](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api/#tag/Pagination).<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of records returned. Default is `20`.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A resource ID to seek from.<br>Returns records created after the specified record;<br>results don't include the specified record.<br><br>Use `after` instead of the `offset` parameter.<br>For more information about pagination parameters, see [Pagination](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api/#tag/Pagination).<br>|
|org|query|string|false|An organization name.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Lists buckets for the organization associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Lists buckets for the specified organization.<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Lists buckets for the organization associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Requires either the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Lists buckets for the specified organization.<br>|
|name|query|string|false|A bucket name.<br>Only returns buckets with the specified name.<br>|
|id|query|string|false|A bucket ID.<br>Only returns the bucket with the specified ID.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {
    "self": "/api/v2/buckets?descending=false&limit=20&name=_monitoring&offset=0&orgID=ORG_ID"
  },
  "buckets": [
    {
      "id": "77ca9dace40a9bfc",
      "orgID": "INFLUX_ORG_ID",
      "type": "system",

        {
          "type": "expire",
          "everySeconds": 604800
        }
      ],

      "updatedAt": "2022-03-15T17:22:33.726179487Z",
      "links": {
        "labels": "/api/v2/buckets/77ca9dace40a9bfc/labels",
        "members": "/api/v2/buckets/77ca9dace40a9bfc/members",
        "org": "/api/v2/orgs/INFLUX_ORG_ID",
        "owners": "/api/v2/buckets/77ca9dace40a9bfc/owners",
        "self": "/api/v2/buckets/77ca9dace40a9bfc",
        "write": "/api/v2/write?org=ORG_ID&bucket=77ca9dace40a9bfc"
      },
      "labels": []
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create a bucket

<a id="opIdPostBuckets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/buckets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "orgID": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "rp": "0",
    "retentionRules": [
      {
        "type": "expire",
        "everySeconds": 86400,
        "shardGroupDurationSeconds": 0
      }
    ],
    "schemaType": "implicit"
  }'
```

`POST /buckets`

Creates a [bucket](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#bucket)
and returns the bucket resource.
The default data
[retention period](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#retention-period)
is 30 days.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- A single InfluxDB OSS instance supports active writes or queries for
approximately 20 buckets across all organizations at a given time.
Reading or writing to more than 20 buckets at a time can adversely affect
performance.

#### Limitations

- InfluxDB Cloud Free Plan allows users to create up to two buckets.
Exceeding the bucket quota will result in an HTTP `403` status code.
For additional information regarding InfluxDB Cloud offerings, see
[InfluxDB Cloud Pricing](https://www.influxdata.com/influxdb-cloud-pricing/).

#### Related Guides

- [Create a bucket](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/buckets/create-bucket/)
- [Create bucket CLI reference](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/cli/influx/bucket/create)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "orgID": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "rp": "0",
  "retentionRules": [
    {
      "type": "expire",
      "everySeconds": 86400,
      "shardGroupDurationSeconds": 0
    }
  ],
  "schemaType": "implicit"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|body|body|[PostBucketRequest](#schemapostbucketrequest)|true|The bucket to create.|
|» orgID|body|string|true|The organization ID.<br>Specifies the organization that owns the bucket.<br>|
|» name|body|string|true|The bucket name.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the bucket.<br>|
|» rp|body|string|false|The retention policy for the bucket.<br>For InfluxDB 1.x, specifies the duration of time that each data point<br>in the retention policy persists.<br><br>If you need compatibility with InfluxDB 1.x, specify a value for the `rp` property;<br>otherwise, see the `retentionRules` property.<br><br>[Retention policy](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1.8/concepts/glossary/#retention-policy-rp)<br>is an InfluxDB 1.x concept.<br>The InfluxDB 2.x and Cloud equivalent is<br>[retention period](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#retention-period).<br>The InfluxDB `/api/v2` API uses `RetentionRules` to configure the retention period.<br>|
|» retentionRules|body|[RetentionRules](#schemaretentionrules)|false|Retention rules to expire or retain data.<br>The InfluxDB `/api/v2` API uses `RetentionRules` to configure the [retention period](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#retention-period).<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- `retentionRules` is required.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- `retentionRules` isn't required.<br>|
|» schemaType|body|[SchemaType](#schemaschematype)|false|The schema Type. Default is `implicit`.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Use `explicit` to enforce column names, tags, fields, and data types for<br>your data.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Doesn't support `explicit` bucket schemas.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» schemaType|implicit|
|» schemaType|explicit|

## Delete a bucket

<a id="opIdDeleteBucketsID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/buckets/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /buckets/{bucketID}`

Deletes a bucket and all associated records.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Does the following when you send a delete request:

  1. Validates the request and queues the delete.
  2. Returns an HTTP `204` status code if queued; _error_ otherwise.
  3. Handles the delete asynchronously.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- Validates the request, handles the delete synchronously,
and then responds with success or failure.

#### Limitations

- Only one bucket can be deleted per request.

#### Related Guides

- [Delete a bucket](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/buckets/delete-bucket/#delete-a-bucket-in-the-influxdb-ui)


<h3 id="delete-a-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|bucketID|path|string|true|Bucket ID.<br>The ID of the bucket to delete.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "id must have a length of 16 bytes"
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
  "code": "not found",

}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|

## Update a bucket

<a id="opIdPatchBucketsID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/buckets/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \

    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "retentionRules": [
      {
        "type": "expire",
        "everySeconds": 86400,
        "shardGroupDurationSeconds": 0
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /buckets/{bucketID}`

Updates a bucket.

Use this endpoint to update properties
(`name`, `description`, and `retentionRules`) of a bucket.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Requires the `retentionRules` property in the request body. If you don't
provide `retentionRules`, InfluxDB responds with an HTTP `403` status code.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- Doesn't require `retentionRules`.

#### Related Guides

- [Update a bucket](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/buckets/update-bucket/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "retentionRules": [
    {
      "type": "expire",
      "everySeconds": 86400,
      "shardGroupDurationSeconds": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|bucketID|path|string|true|The bucket ID.|
|body|body|[PatchBucketRequest](#schemapatchbucketrequest)|true|The bucket update to apply.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the bucket.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the bucket.<br>|
|» retentionRules|body|[PatchRetentionRules](#schemapatchretentionrules)|false|Updates to rules to expire or retain data. No rules means no updates.|

## List all labels for a bucket

<a id="opIdGetBucketsIDLabels"></a>

`GET /buckets/{bucketID}/labels`

Lists all labels for a bucket.

Labels are objects that contain `labelID`, `name`, `description`, and `color`
key-value pairs. They may be used for grouping and filtering InfluxDB
resources.
Labels are also capable of grouping across different resources--for example,
you can apply a label named `air_sensor` to a bucket and a task to quickly
organize resources.

#### Related guides

## Add a label to a bucket

<a id="opIdPostBucketsIDLabels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/buckets/string/labels \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "labelID": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /buckets/{bucketID}/labels`

Adds a label to a bucket and returns the new label information.

Labels are objects that contain `labelID`, `name`, `description`, and `color`
key-value pairs. They may be used for grouping and filtering across one or
more kinds of **resources**--for example, you can apply a label named
`air_sensor` to a bucket and a task to quickly organize resources.

#### Limitations

- Before adding a label to a bucket, you must create the label if you
  haven't already. To create a label with the InfluxDB API, send a `POST`
  request to the [`/api/v2/labels` endpoint](#operation/PostLabels)).

#### Related guides

- Use the [`/api/v2/labels` InfluxDB API endpoint](#tag/Labels) to retrieve and manage labels.
- [Manage labels in the InfluxDB UI](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/visualize-data/labels/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "labelID": "string"
}
```

|body|body|[LabelMapping](#schemalabelmapping)|true|An object that contains a _`labelID`_ to add to the bucket.|
|» labelID|body|string|true|A label ID.<br>Specifies the label to attach.<br>|

## List all owners of a bucket

<a id="opIdGetBucketsIDOwners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/buckets/string/owners \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /buckets/{bucketID}/owners`

Lists all [owners](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#owner)
of a bucket.

Bucket owners have permission to delete buckets and remove user and member
permissions from the bucket.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Doesn't use `owner` and `member` roles.
  Use [`/api/v2/authorizations`](#tag/Authorizations-(API-tokens)) to assign user permissions.

#### Limitations

- Owner permissions are separate from API token permissions.
- Owner permissions are used in the context of the InfluxDB UI.

#### Required permissions

- `read-orgs INFLUX_ORG_ID`

*`INFLUX_ORG_ID`* is the ID of the organization that you want to retrieve a
list of owners for.

#### Related endpoints

- [Authorizations](#tag/Authorizations-(API-tokens))

#### Related guides

- [Manage users](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/users/)


<h3 id="list-all-owners-of-a-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## Add an owner to a bucket

<a id="opIdPostBucketsIDOwners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/buckets/string/owners \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "role": "owner",
    "links": {
      "self": "/api/v2/users/d88d182d91b0950f"
    },
    "id": "d88d182d91b0950f",
    "name": "example-user",
    "status": "active"
  }'
```

`POST /buckets/{bucketID}/owners`

Adds an owner to a bucket and returns the [owners](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#owner)
with role and user detail.

Use this endpoint to create a _resource owner_ for the bucket.
Bucket owners have permission to delete buckets and remove user and member
permissions from the bucket.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Doesn't use `owner` and `member` roles.
  Use [`/api/v2/authorizations`](#tag/Authorizations-(API-tokens)) to assign user permissions.

#### Limitations

- Owner permissions are separate from API token permissions.
- Owner permissions are used in the context of the InfluxDB UI.

#### Required permissions

- `write-orgs INFLUX_ORG_ID`
*`INFLUX_ORG_ID`* is the ID of the organization that you want to add
  an owner for.

#### Related endpoints

- [Authorizations](#tag/Authorizations-(API-tokens))

#### Related guides

- [Manage users](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/users/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "role": "owner",
  "links": {
    "self": "/api/v2/users/d88d182d91b0950f"
  },
  "id": "d88d182d91b0950f",
  "name": "example-user",
  "status": "active"
}
```

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-dbrps">DBRPs</h1>

The InfluxDB 1.x data model includes [databases](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1.8/concepts/glossary/#database)
and [retention policies](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1.8/concepts/glossary/#retention-policy-rp).
InfluxDB 2.x replaces databases and retention policies with buckets.
To support InfluxDB 1.x query and write patterns in InfluxDB 2.x,
databases and retention policies are mapped to buckets using the
database and retention policy (DBRP) mapping service.
The DBRP mapping service uses the database and retention policy
specified in 1.x compatibility API requests to route operations to a bucket.

### Related guides

- [Database and retention policy mapping](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/api/influxdb-1x/dbrp/)


## List database retention policy mappings

<a id="opIdGetDBRPs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/dbrps \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /dbrps`

Lists database retention policy (DBRP) mappings.

#### Related guide

- [Database and retention policy mapping](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/api/influxdb-1x/dbrp/)


<h3 id="list-database-retention-policy-mappings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID.<br>Only returns DBRP mappings for the specified organization.<br>|
|org|query|string|false|An organization name.<br>Only returns DBRP mappings for the specified organization.<br>|
|id|query|string|false|A DBPR mapping ID.<br>Only returns the specified DBRP mapping.<br>|
|bucketID|query|string|false|A bucket ID.<br>Only returns DBRP mappings that belong to the specified bucket.<br>|
|default|query|boolean|false|Specifies filtering on default|
|db|query|string|false|A database.<br>Only returns DBRP mappings that belong to the 1.x database.<br>|
|rp|query|string|false|A [retention policy](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1.8/concepts/glossary/#retention-policy-rp).<br>Specifies the 1.x retention policy to filter on.<br>|

## Add a database retention policy mapping

<a id="opIdPostDBRP"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/dbrps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "org": "string",
    "orgID": "string",
    "bucketID": "string",
    "database": "string",
    "retention_policy": "string",
    "default": true
  }'
```

`POST /dbrps`

Creates a database retention policy (DBRP) mapping and returns the mapping.

Use this endpoint to add InfluxDB 1.x API compatibility to your
InfluxDB Cloud or InfluxDB OSS 2.x buckets. Your buckets must contain a
DBRP mapping in order to query and write using the InfluxDB 1.x API.
object.

#### Related guide

- [Database and retention policy mapping](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/api/influxdb-1x/dbrp/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "org": "string",
  "orgID": "string",
  "bucketID": "string",
  "database": "string",
  "retention_policy": "string",
  "default": true
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-database-retention-policy-mapping-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|body|body|[DBRPCreate](#schemadbrpcreate)|true|The database retention policy mapping to add.<br><br>Note that _`retention_policy`_ is a required parameter in the request body.<br>The value of _`retention_policy`_ can be any arbitrary `string` name or<br>value, with the default value commonly set as `autogen`.<br>The value of _`retention_policy`_ isn't a [retention_policy](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#retention-policy-rp)<br>|
|» org|body|string|false|An organization name.<br>Identifies the [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization) that owns the mapping.<br>|
|» orgID|body|string|false|An organization ID.<br>Identifies the [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization) that owns the mapping.<br>|
|» bucketID|body|string|true|A bucket ID.<br>Identifies the bucket used as the target for the translation.<br>|
|» database|body|string|true|A database name.<br>Identifies the InfluxDB v1 database.<br>|
|» retention_policy|body|string|true|A [retention policy](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1.8/concepts/glossary/#retention-policy-rp) name.<br>Identifies the InfluxDB v1 retention policy mapping.<br>|
|» default|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to use this DBRP mapping as the default retention policy<br>for the database (specified by the `database` property's value).<br>|

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-debug">Debug</h1>

Generate profiling and trace reports.

Use routes under `/debug/pprof` to analyze the Go runtime of InfluxDB.
These endpoints generate [Go runtime profiles](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof)
and **trace** reports.
**Profiles** are collections of stack traces that show call sequences
leading to instances of a particular event, such as allocation.

For more information about **pprof profile** and **trace** reports,
see the following resources:

- [Google pprof tool](https://github.com/google/pprof)
- [Golang diagnostics](https://go.dev/doc/diagnostics)


## Retrieve all runtime profiles

<a id="opIdGetDebugPprofAllProfiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/debug/pprof/all \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /debug/pprof/all`

Collects samples and returns reports for the following [Go runtime profiles](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof):

- **allocs**: All past memory allocations
- **block**: Stack traces that led to blocking on synchronization primitives
- **cpu**: (Optional) Program counters sampled from the executing stack.
  Include by passing the `cpu` query parameter with a [duration](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#duration) value.
  Equivalent to the report from [`GET /debug/pprof/profile?seconds=NUMBER_OF_SECONDS`](#operation/GetDebugPprofProfile).
- **goroutine**: All current goroutines
- **heap**: Memory allocations for live objects
- **mutex**: Holders of contended mutexes
- **threadcreate**: Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads


<h3 id="retrieve-all-runtime-profiles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|cpu|query|string(duration)|false|Collects and returns CPU profiling data for the specified [duration](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#duration).<br>|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-all-runtime-profiles-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|[Go runtime profile](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof) reports.<br>|Inline|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

## Retrieve the memory allocations runtime profile

<a id="opIdGetDebugPprofAllocs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/debug/pprof/allocs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /debug/pprof/allocs`

Returns a [Go runtime profile](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof) report of
all past memory allocations.
**allocs** is the same as the **heap** profile,
but changes the default [pprof](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof)
display to __-alloc_space__,
the total number of bytes allocated since the program began (including garbage-collected bytes).


<h3 id="retrieve-the-memory-allocations-runtime-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|debug|query|integer(int64)|false|- `0`: (Default) Return the report as a gzip-compressed protocol buffer.<br>- `1`: Return a response body with the report formatted as human-readable text.<br>  The report contains comments that translate addresses to function names and line numbers for debugging.<br><br>`debug=1` is mutually exclusive with the `seconds` query parameter.<br>|
|seconds|query|string(int64)|false|Number of seconds to collect statistics.<br><br>`seconds` is mutually exclusive with `debug=1`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|debug|0|
|debug|1|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-the-memory-allocations-runtime-profile-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|[Go runtime profile](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof) report compatible<br>with [pprof](https://github.com/google/pprof) analysis and visualization tools.<br>If debug is enabled (`?debug=1`), response body contains a human-readable profile.<br>|Inline|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

`GET /debug/pprof/heap`

Collects statistics and returns a [Go runtime profile](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/pprof)

To run **garbage collection** before sampling,

|seconds|query|string(int64)|false|Number of seconds to collect statistics.<br><br>`seconds` is mutually exclusive with `debug=1`.<br>|
|gc|query|integer(int64)|false|- `0`: (Default) don't force garbage collection before sampling.<br>- `1`: Force garbage collection before sampling.<br>|

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-organizations">Organizations</h1>

Create and manage your [organizations](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization).
An organization is a workspace for a group of users. Organizations can be
used to separate different environments, projects, teams or users within
InfluxDB.

Use the `/api/v2/orgs` endpoints to create, view, and manage organizations.


## List organizations

<a id="opIdGetOrgs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/orgs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /orgs`

Lists [organizations](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization/).

To limit which organizations are returned, pass query parameters in your request.
If no query parameters are passed, InfluxDB returns all organizations up to the default `limit`.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Only returns the organization that owns the token passed in the request.

#### Related guides

- [View organizations](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/view-orgs/)


<h3 id="list-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|offset|query|integer|false|The offset for pagination.<br>The number of records to skip.<br><br>For more information about pagination parameters, see [Pagination](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api/#tag/Pagination).<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of records returned. Default is `20`.<br>|
|descending|query|boolean|false|none|
|org|query|string|false|An organization name.<br>Only returns the specified organization.<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID.<br>Only returns the specified organization.<br>|
|userID|query|string|false|A user ID.<br>Only returns organizations where the specified user is a member or owner.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {
    "self": "/api/v2/orgs"
  },
  "orgs": [
    {
      "links": {
        "buckets": "/api/v2/buckets?org=INFLUX_ORG",
        "dashboards": "/api/v2/dashboards?org=INFLUX_ORG",
        "labels": "/api/v2/orgs/INFLUX_ORG_ID/labels",
        "logs": "/api/v2/orgs/INFLUX_ORG_ID/logs",
        "members": "/api/v2/orgs/INFLUX_ORG_ID/members",
        "owners": "/api/v2/orgs/INFLUX_ORG_ID/owners",
        "secrets": "/api/v2/orgs/INFLUX_ORG_ID/secrets",
        "self": "/api/v2/orgs/INFLUX_ORG_ID",

      },
      "id": "INFLUX_ORG_ID",
      "name": "INFLUX_ORG",
      "description": "Example InfluxDB organization",
      "createdAt": "2022-07-17T23:00:30.778487Z",
      "updatedAt": "2022-07-17T23:00:30.778487Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Delete an organization

<a id="opIdDeleteOrgsID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/orgs/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /orgs/{orgID}`

Deletes an organization.

Deleting an organization from InfluxDB Cloud can't be undone.
Once deleted, all data associated with the organization is removed.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Does the following when you send a delete request:

  1. Validates the request and queues the delete.
  2. Returns an HTTP `204` status code if queued; _error_ otherwise.
  3. Handles the delete asynchronously.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- Validates the request, handles the delete synchronously,
and then responds with success or failure.

#### Limitations

- Only one organization can be deleted per request.

#### Related guides

- [Delete organizations](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/delete-orgs/)


<h3 id="delete-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|orgID|path|string|true|The ID of the organization to delete.<br>|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "failed to decode request body: organization not found"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "not found",
  "message": "org not found"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br>  - The organization is queued for deletion.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br>  - The organization is deleted.<br>|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.<br>The response body contains detail about the error.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Returns this error if an incorrect value is passed in the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found.<br>InfluxDB can't find the organization.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **401**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|message|string|false|read-only|A human-readable message that may contain detail about the error.|

#### Enumerated Values

`PATCH /orgs/{orgID}`

- Dashboards

- Telegraf configurations

If you change an organization name, be sure to update the organization name
in these resources as well.

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /orgs/{orgID}/members`

Lists all users that belong to an organization.

InfluxDB [users](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user) have
permission to access InfluxDB.

[Members](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#member) are users
within the organization.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Doesn't use `owner` and `member` roles.
  Use [`/api/v2/authorizations`](#tag/Authorizations-(API-tokens)) to assign user permissions.

#### Limitations

- Member permissions are separate from API token permissions.
- Member permissions are used in the context of the InfluxDB UI.

#### Required permissions

- `read-orgs INFLUX_ORG_ID`

*`INFLUX_ORG_ID`* is the ID of the organization that you want to retrieve
members for.

#### Related guides

- [Manage users](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/users/)
- [Manage members](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/members/)

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-query">Query</h1>

Retrieve data, analyze queries, and get query suggestions.


## Generate a query Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)

<a id="opIdPostQueryAst"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/query/ast \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "query": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /query/ast`

Analyzes a Flux query and returns a complete package source [Abstract Syntax
Tree (AST)](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#abstract-syntax-tree-ast)
for the query.

Use this endpoint for deep query analysis such as debugging unexpected query
results.

A Flux query AST provides a semantic, tree-like representation with contextual
information about the query. The AST illustrates how the query is distributed
into different components for execution.

#### Limitations

-  The endpoint doesn't validate values in the query--for example:

    The following sample Flux query has correct syntax, but contains an incorrect `from()` property key:

    ```js
    from(foo: "iot_center")
        |> range(start: -90d)
        |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "environment")
    ```

    The following sample JSON shows how to pass the query in the request body:

    ```js
    from(foo: "iot_center")
    |> range(start: -90d)
    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "environment")
    ```

    The following code sample shows how to pass the query as JSON in the request body:

    ```json
    { "query": "from(foo: \"iot_center\")\
                    |> range(start: -90d)\
                    |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == \"environment\")"
    }
    ```

    Passing this to `/api/v2/query/ast` will return a successful response
    with a generated AST.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "query": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-query-abstract-syntax-tree-ast-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|Content-Type|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[LanguageRequest](#schemalanguagerequest)|false|The Flux query to analyze.|
|» query|body|string|true|The Flux query script to be analyzed.<br>|

<h3 id="generate-a-query-abstract-syntax-tree-ast-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.<br>The response body contains an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) of the Flux query.<br>|[ASTResponse](#schemaastresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.<br>InfluxDB is unable to parse the request.<br>The response body contains detail about the problem.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Internal server error.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|400|X-Platform-Error-Code|string||The reason for the error.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

## List Flux query suggestions

<a id="opIdGetQuerySuggestions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/query/suggestions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /query/suggestions`

Lists Flux query suggestions. Each suggestion contains a
[Flux function](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/stdlib/all-functions/)
name and parameters.

Use this endpoint to retrieve a list of Flux query suggestions used in the
InfluxDB Flux Query Builder.

#### Limitations

- When writing a query, avoid using `_functionName()` helper functions
exposed by this endpoint.  Helper function names have an underscore (`_`)
prefix and aren't meant to be used directly in queries--for example:

  - To sort on a column and keep the top n records, use the
    `top(n, columns=["_value"], tables=<-)` function instead of the `_sortLimit`
    helper function. `top` uses `_sortLimit`.

#### Related Guides

- [List of all Flux functions](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/stdlib/all-functions/)


<h3 id="list-flux-query-suggestions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

## Retrieve a query suggestion for a branching suggestion

<a id="opIdGetQuerySuggestionsName"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/query/suggestions/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /query/suggestions/{name}`

Retrieves a query suggestion that contains the name and parameters of the
requested function.

Use this endpoint to pass a branching suggestion (a Flux function name) and
retrieve the parameters of the requested function.

#### Limitations

- Use `/api/v2/query/suggestions/{name}` (without a trailing slash).
`/api/v2/query/suggestions/{name}/` (note the trailing slash) results in a
HTTP `301 Moved Permanently` status.

- The function `name` must exist and must be spelled correctly.

#### Related Guides

- [List of all Flux functions](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/stdlib/all-functions/)


<h3 id="retrieve-a-query-suggestion-for-a-branching-suggestion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|name|path|string|true|A [Flux function](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/stdlib/all-functions/) name.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "name": "sum",
  "params": {
    "column": "string",
    "tables": "stream"
  }
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "An internal error has occurred"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-query-suggestion-for-a-branching-suggestion-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.<br>The response body contains the function name and parameters.<br>|[FluxSuggestion](#schemafluxsuggestion)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The value passed for _`name`_ may have been misspelled.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

## Analyze a Flux query

<a id="opIdPostQueryAnalyze"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/query/analyze \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "extern": {
      "type": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "package": {
        "type": "string",
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "name": "string"
        }
      },
      "imports": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "as": {
            "type": "string",
            "name": "string"
          },
          "path": {
            "type": "string",
            "value": "string"
          }
        }
      ],
      "body": [
        {
          "type": "string",
          "text": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "query": "string",
    "type": "flux",
    "params": {},
    "dialect": {
      "header": true,
      "delimiter": ",",
      "annotations": [
        "group"
      ],
      "commentPrefix": "#",
      "dateTimeFormat": "RFC3339"
    },
    "now": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /query/analyze`

Analyzes a [Flux query](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/) for syntax
errors and returns the list of errors.

In the following sample query, `from()` is missing the property key.

    ```json
    { "query": "from(: \"iot_center\")\
                |> range(start: -90d)\
                |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == \"environment\")",
      "type": "flux"
    }
    ```

If you pass this in a request to the `/api/v2/analyze` endpoint,
InfluxDB returns an `errors` list that contains an error object for the missing key.

#### Limitations

-  The endpoint doesn't validate values in the query--for example:

  - The following sample query has correct syntax, but contains an incorrect `from()` property key:

    ```json
    { "query": "from(foo: \"iot_center\")\
                |> range(start: -90d)\
                |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == \"environment\")",
      "type": "flux"
    }
    ```

    If you pass this in a request to the `/api/v2/analyze` endpoint,
    InfluxDB returns an empty `errors` list.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "extern": {
    "type": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "package": {
      "type": "string",
      "name": {
        "type": "string",
        "name": "string"
      }
    },
    "imports": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "as": {
          "type": "string",
          "name": "string"
        },
        "path": {
          "type": "string",
          "value": "string"
        }
      }
    ],
    "body": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "text": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "query": "string",
  "type": "flux",
  "params": {},
  "dialect": {
    "header": true,
    "delimiter": ",",
    "annotations": [
      "group"
    ],
    "commentPrefix": "#",
    "dateTimeFormat": "RFC3339"
  },
  "now": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="analyze-a-flux-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|Content-Type|header|string|false|none|
|body|body|[Query](#schemaquery)|false|Flux query to analyze|
|» extern|body|[File](#schemafile)|false|Represents a source from a single file|
|» query|body|string|true|The query script to execute.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of query. Must be "flux".|
|» params|body|object|false|Key-value pairs passed as parameters during query execution.<br><br>To use parameters in your query, pass a _`query`_ with `params` references (in dot notation)--for example:<br><br>```json<br>  query: "from(bucket: params.mybucket)\<br>              \|> range(start: params.rangeStart) \|> limit(n:1)"<br>```<br><br>and pass _`params`_ with the key-value pairs--for example:<br><br>```json<br>  params: {<br>    "mybucket": "environment",<br>    "rangeStart": "-30d"<br>  }<br>```<br><br>During query execution, InfluxDB passes _`params`_ to your script and substitutes the values.<br><br>#### Limitations<br><br>- If you use _`params`_, you can't use _`extern`_.<br>|
|» dialect|body|[Dialect](#schemadialect)|false|Options for tabular data output.<br>Default output is [annotated CSV](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/annotated-csv/#csv-response-format) with headers.<br><br>For more information about tabular data **dialect**,<br>see [W3 metadata vocabulary for tabular data](https://www.w3.org/TR/2015/REC-tabular-metadata-20151217/#dialect-descriptions).<br>|
|» now|body|string(date-time)|false|Specifies the time that should be reported as `now` in the query.<br>Default is the server `now` time.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Type|application/json|
|» type|flux|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "line": 1,
      "column": 6,
      "character": 0,
      "message": "missing property key"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "invalid json: invalid character '\\'' looking for beginning of value"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "An internal error has occurred - check server logs"
}
```

<h3 id="analyze-a-flux-query-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.<br>The response body contains the list of `errors`.<br>If the query syntax is valid, the endpoint returns an empty `errors` list.<br>|[AnalyzeQueryResponse](#schemaanalyzequeryresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.<br>InfluxDB is unable to parse the request.<br>The response body contains detail about the problem.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Internal server error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|400|X-Platform-Error-Code|string||The reason for the error.<br>|
|default|X-Platform-Error-Code|string||The reason for the error.|
|default|X-Influx-Error|string||A string that describes the problem.|
|default|X-Influx-Reference|integer||The numeric reference code for the error type.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-tasks">Tasks</h1>

Process and analyze your data with [tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task)
in the InfluxDB task engine.
Use the `/api/v2/tasks` endpoints to schedule and manage tasks, retry task runs, and retrieve run logs.

To configure a task, provide the script and the schedule to run the task.
For examples, see how to create a task with the [`POST /api/v2/tasks` endpoint](#operation/PostTasks).

<span id="tasks-schemaref-task" />

### Properties

A `task` object contains information about an InfluxDB task resource.

The following table defines the properties that appear in a `task` object:

<SchemaDefinition schemaRef="#/components/schemas/Task" />

### Related guides

- [Get started with tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/get-started/)
- [Common data processing tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/common-tasks/)


## List runs for a task

<a id="opIdGetTasksIDRuns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks/string/runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /tasks/{taskID}/runs`

Retrieves a list of runs for a [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/).

To limit which task runs are returned, pass query parameters in your request.
If no query parameters are passed, InfluxDB returns all task runs up to the default `limit`.


<h3 id="list-runs-for-a-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|taskID|path|string|true|The ID of the task to get runs for.<br>Only returns runs for this task.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A task run ID. Only returns runs created after this run.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of task runs returned. Default is `100`.<br>|
|afterTime|query|string(date-time)|false|A timestamp ([RFC3339 date/time format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp)).<br>Only returns runs scheduled after this time.<br>|
|beforeTime|query|string(date-time)|false|A timestamp ([RFC3339 date/time format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp)).<br>Only returns runs scheduled before this time.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com"
  },
  "runs": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "taskID": "string",
      "status": "scheduled",
      "scheduledFor": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "log": [
        {
          "time": "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00",
          "message": "Halt and catch fire",
          "runID": "string"
        }
      ],
      "flux": "string",
      "startedAt": "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00",
      "finishedAt": "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00",
      "requestedAt": "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00",
      "links": {
        "self": "/api/v2/tasks/1/runs/1",
        "task": "/api/v2/tasks/1",
        "retry": "/api/v2/tasks/1/runs/1/retry"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-runs-for-a-task-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success. The response body contains the list of task runs.|[Runs](#schemaruns)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-runs-for-a-task-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **401**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|read-only|The HTTP status code description. Default is `unauthorized`.<br>|
|message|string|false|read-only|A human-readable message that may contain detail about the error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|unauthorized|

## Retrieve a run for a task.

<a id="opIdGetTasksIDRunsID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks/string/runs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /tasks/{taskID}/runs/{runID}`

Retrieves a specific run for a [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task).

Use this endpoint to retrieve detail and logs for a specific task run.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-run-for-a-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|taskID|path|string|true|The ID of the task to retrieve runs for.|
|runID|path|string|true|The ID of the run to retrieve.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {
    "logs": "/api/v2/tasks/0996e56b2f378000/runs/09b070dadaa7d000/logs",
    "retry": "/api/v2/tasks/0996e56b2f378000/runs/09b070dadaa7d000/retry",
    "self": "/api/v2/tasks/0996e56b2f378000/runs/09b070dadaa7d000",
```

## Cancel a running task

<a id="opIdDeleteTasksIDRunsID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks/string/runs/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /tasks/{taskID}/runs/{runID}`

Cancels a running [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task).

Use this endpoint with InfluxDB OSS to cancel a running task.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Doesn't support this operation.


<h3 id="cancel-a-running-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|taskID|path|string|true|The ID of the task to cancel.|
|runID|path|string|true|The ID of the task run to cancel.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "failed to decode request body: organization not found"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "not found",
  "message": "organization name \"my-org\" not found"
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-running-task-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success. The `DELETE` is accepted and the run will be cancelled.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't support this operation.<br>- Doesn't return this status.<br>|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.<br>The response body contains detail about the error.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Returns this error if an incorrect value is passed in the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found.<br>A requested resource was not found.<br>The response body contains the requested resource type and the name value<br>(if you passed it)--for example:<br><br>- `"organization name \"my-org\" not found"`<br>- `"organization not found"`: indicates you passed an ID that did not match<br>   an organization.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Method not allowed.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>  - Always returns this error; doesn't support cancelling tasks.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>  - Doesn't return this error.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

## Retry a task run

<a id="opIdPostTasksIDRunsIDRetry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks/string/runs/string/retry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /tasks/{taskID}/runs/{runID}/retry`

Queues a [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task)  run to
retry and returns the scheduled run.

To manually start a _new_ task run, use the
[`POST /api/v2/tasks/{taskID}/runs` endpoint](#operation/PostTasksIDRuns).

#### Limitations

- The task must be _active_ (`status: "active"`).


> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="retry-a-task-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|taskID|path|string|true|A [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task)  ID.<br>Specifies the task to retry.<br>|
|runID|path|string|true|A [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task) run ID.<br>Specifies the task run to retry.<br><br>To find a task run ID, use the<br>[`GET /api/v2/tasks/{taskID}/runs` endpoint](#operation/GetTasksIDRuns)<br>to list task runs.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|

```json
    "self": "/api/v2/tasks/09a776832f381000/runs/09d60ffe08738000",
    "task": "/api/v2/tasks/09a776832f381000"
  },
  "id": "09d60ffe08738000",
  "taskID": "09a776832f381000",
  "status": "scheduled",
  "scheduledFor": "2022-08-15T00:00:00Z",
  "requestedAt": "2022-08-16T20:05:11.84145Z"
}
```

```json
{
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "failed to retry run: inactive task"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json

  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "code": "not found",
  "message": "organization name \"my-org\" not found"
}
```

```json
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

```json
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
```

## Retrieve all logs for a task

<a id="opIdGetTasksIDLogs"></a>

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks/string/logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /tasks/{taskID}/logs`

Retrieves a list of all logs for a [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task).

When an InfluxDB task runs, a “run” record is created in the task’s history.
Logs associated with each run provide relevant log messages, timestamps, and the exit status of the run attempt.

Use this endpoint to retrieve only the log events for a task,
without additional task metadata.

```json
    {
      "runID": "09b070dadaa7d000",
      "time": "2022-07-18T14:46:07.242859Z",
      "message": "Completed(success)"
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /tasks/{taskID}/labels`

```json
{
  "labelID": "string"
}
```

|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

|body|body|[LabelMapping](#schemalabelmapping)|true|An object that contains a _`labelID`_ to add to the task.|
|» labelID|body|string|true|A label ID.<br>Specifies the label to attach.<br>|

```json
{
```
