## Update a task

<a id="opIdPatchTasksID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "status": "active",
    "flux": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "every": "string",
    "cron": "string",
    "offset": "string",
    "description": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /tasks/{taskID}`

Updates a task and then cancels all scheduled runs of the task.

Use this endpoint to set, modify, and clear task properties (for example: `cron`, `name`, `flux`, `status`).
Once InfluxDB applies the update, it cancels all previously scheduled runs of the task.

To update a task, pass an object that contains the updated key-value pairs.
To activate or inactivate a task, set the `status` property.
_`"status": "inactive"`_ cancels scheduled runs and prevents manual runs of the task.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "status": "active",
  "flux": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "every": "string",
  "cron": "string",
  "offset": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|taskID|path|string|true|The ID of the task to update.|
|body|body|[TaskUpdateRequest](#schemataskupdaterequest)|true|An object that contains updated task properties to apply.|
|» status|body|[TaskStatusType](#schemataskstatustype)|false|`inactive` cancels scheduled runs and prevents manual runs of the task.<br>|
|» flux|body|string|false|The Flux script that the task runs.|

|» offset|body|string|false|Update the 'offset' option in the flux script.|
|» description|body|string|false|Update the description of the task.|

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-templates">Templates</h1>

Export and apply InfluxDB **templates**.
Manage **stacks** of templated InfluxDB resources.

InfluxDB templates are prepackaged configurations for
everything from dashboards and Telegraf to notifications and alerts.
Use InfluxDB templates to quickly configure a fresh instance of InfluxDB,
back up your dashboard configuration, or share your configuration with the
InfluxData community.

Use the `/api/v2/templates` endpoints to export templates and apply templates.

**InfluxDB stacks** are stateful InfluxDB templates that let you
add, update, and remove installed template resources over time, avoid duplicating
resources when applying the same or similar templates more than once, and
apply changes to distributed instances of InfluxDB OSS or InfluxDB Cloud.

Use the `/api/v2/stacks` endpoints to manage installed template resources.

### Related guides

- [InfluxDB stacks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/)
- [InfluxDB templates](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/)


## List installed stacks

<a id="opIdListStacks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8086/stacks?orgID=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /stacks`

Lists installed InfluxDB stacks.

To limit stacks in the response, pass query parameters in your request.
If no query parameters are passed, InfluxDB returns all installed stacks
for the organization.

#### Related guides

- [View InfluxDB stacks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/).

|name|query|string|false|A stack name.<br>Finds stack `events` with this name and returns the stacks.<br><br>Repeatable.<br>To filter for more than one stack name,<br>repeat this parameter with each name--for example:<br><br>- `INFLUX_URL/api/v2/stacks?&orgID=INFLUX_ORG_ID&name=project-stack-0&name=project-stack-1`<br>|
|stackID|query|string|false|A stack ID.<br>Only returns the specified stack.<br><br>Repeatable.<br>To filter for more than one stack ID,<br>repeat this parameter with each ID--for example:<br><br>- `INFLUX_URL/api/v2/stacks?&orgID=INFLUX_ORG_ID&stackID=09bd87cd33be3000&stackID=09bef35081fe3000`<br>|

## Create a stack

<a id="opIdCreateStack"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/stacks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{

      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /stacks`

Creates or initializes a stack.

Use this endpoint to _manually_ initialize a new stack with the following
optional information:

  - Stack name
  - Stack description
  - URLs for template manifest files

To automatically create a stack when applying templates,
use the [/api/v2/templates/apply endpoint](#operation/ApplyTemplate).

#### Required permissions

- `write` permission for the organization

#### Related guides

- [Initialize an InfluxDB stack](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/init/).
- [Use InfluxDB templates](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/#apply-templates-to-an-influxdb-instance).

## Apply or dry-run a template

<a id="opIdApplyTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/templates/apply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "orgID": "INFLUX_ORG_ID",
    "actions": [
      {
        "action": "skipKind",
        "properties": {
          "kind": "Bucket"
        }
      },
      {
        "action": "skipKind",
        "properties": {
          "kind": "Task"
        }
      }
    ],
    "templates": [
      {
        "contents": [
          {
            "[object Object]": null
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /templates/apply`

Applies a template to
create or update a [stack](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/) of InfluxDB
[resources](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/cli/influx/export/all/#resources).
The response contains the diff of changes and the stack ID.

Use this endpoint to install an InfluxDB template to an organization.
Provide template URLs or template objects in your request.
To customize which template resources are installed, use the `actions`
parameter.

By default, when you apply a template, InfluxDB installs the template to
create and update stack resources and then generates a diff of the changes.
If you pass `dryRun: true` in the request body, InfluxDB validates the
template and generates the resource diff, but doesn’t make any
changes to your instance.

#### Custom values for templates

- Some templates may contain [environment references](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/create/#include-user-definable-resource-names) for custom metadata.
  To provide custom values for environment references, pass the _`envRefs`_
  property in the request body.
  For more information and examples, see how to
  [define environment references](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/#define-environment-references).

- Some templates may contain queries that use
  [secrets](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/secrets/).
  To provide custom secret values, pass the _`secrets`_ property
  in the request body.
  Don't expose secret values in templates.
  For more information, see [how to pass secrets when installing a template](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/#pass-secrets-when-installing-a-template).

#### Required permissions

- `write` permissions for resource types in the template.

#### Rate limits (with InfluxDB Cloud)

- Adjustable service quotas apply.
  For more information, see [limits and adjustable quotas](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/limits/).

#### Related guides

- [Use templates](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/)
- [Stacks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
```

<h3 id="apply-or-dry-run-a-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[TemplateApply](#schematemplateapply)|true|Parameters for applying templates.<br>|
|» dryRun|body|boolean|false|Only applies a dry run of the templates passed in the request.<br><br>- Validates the template and generates a resource diff and summary.<br>- Doesn't install templates or make changes to the InfluxDB instance.<br>|
|» orgID|body|string|false|Organization ID.<br>InfluxDB applies templates to this organization.<br>The organization owns all resources created by the template.<br><br>To find your organization, see how to<br>[view organizations](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/view-orgs/).<br>|
|» stackID|body|string|false|ID of the stack to update.<br><br>To apply templates to an existing stack in the organization, use the `stackID` parameter.<br>If you apply templates without providing a stack ID,<br>InfluxDB initializes a new stack with all new resources.<br><br>To find a stack ID, use the InfluxDB [`/api/v2/stacks` API endpoint](#operation/ListStacks) to list stacks.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [Stacks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/)<br>- [View stacks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/view/)<br>|
|» template|body|object|false|A template object to apply.<br>A template object has a `contents` property<br>with an array of InfluxDB resource configurations.<br><br>Pass `template` to apply only one template object.<br>If you use `template`, you can't use the `templates` parameter.<br>If you want to apply multiple template objects, use `templates` instead.<br>|
|» » contentType|body|string|false|none|
|» » sources|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » contents|body|[Template](#schematemplate)|false|none|
|» templates|body|[object]|false|A list of template objects to apply.<br>A template object has a `contents` property<br>with an array of InfluxDB resource configurations.<br><br>Use the `templates` parameter to apply multiple template objects.<br>If you use `templates`, you can't use the `template` parameter.<br>|
|» » contentType|body|string|false|none|
|» » sources|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » contents|body|[Template](#schematemplate)|false|none|
|» envRefs|body|object|false|An object with key-value pairs that map to **environment references** in templates.<br><br>Environment references in templates are `envRef` objects with an `envRef.key`<br>property.<br>To substitute a custom environment reference value when applying templates,<br>pass `envRefs` with the `envRef.key` and the value.<br><br>When you apply a template, InfluxDB replaces `envRef` objects in the template<br>with the values that you provide in the `envRefs` parameter.<br>For more examples, see how to [define environment references](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/#define-environment-references).<br><br>The following template fields may use environment references:<br><br>  - `metadata.name`<br>  - `spec.endpointName`<br>  - `spec.associations.name`<br><br>For more information about including environment references in template fields, see how to<br>[include user-definable resource names](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/create/#include-user-definable-resource-names).<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string \| integer \| number \| boolean|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|number|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|boolean|false|none|
|» secrets|body|object|false|An object with key-value pairs that map to **secrets** in queries.<br><br>Queries may reference secrets stored in InfluxDB--for example,<br>the following Flux script retrieves `POSTGRES_USERNAME` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`<br>secrets and then uses them to connect to a PostgreSQL database:<br><br>```js<br>import "sql"<br>import "influxdata/influxdb/secrets"<br><br>username = secrets.get(key: "POSTGRES_USERNAME")<br>password = secrets.get(key: "POSTGRES_PASSWORD")<br><br>sql.from(<br>  driverName: "postgres",<br>  dataSourceName: "postgresql://${username}:${password}@localhost:5432",<br>  query: "SELECT * FROM example_table",<br>)<br>```<br><br>To define secret values in your `/api/v2/templates/apply` request,<br>pass the `secrets` parameter with key-value pairs--for example:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  ...<br>  "secrets": {<br>    "POSTGRES_USERNAME": "pguser",<br>    "POSTGRES_PASSWORD": "foo"<br>  }<br>  ...<br>}<br>```<br><br>InfluxDB stores the key-value pairs as secrets that you can access with `secrets.get()`.<br>Once stored, you can't view secret values in InfluxDB.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [How to pass secrets when installing a template](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/#pass-secrets-when-installing-a-template)<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» remotes|body|[object]|false|A list of URLs for template files.<br><br>To apply a template manifest file located at a URL, pass `remotes`<br>with an array that contains the URL.<br>|
|» » url|body|string|true|none|
|» » contentType|body|string|false|none|
|» actions|body|[object]|false|A list of `action` objects.<br>Actions let you customize how InfluxDB applies templates in the request.<br><br>You can use the following actions to prevent creating or updating resources:<br><br>- A `skipKind` action skips template resources of a specified `kind`.<br>- A `skipResource` action skips template resources with a specified `metadata.name`<br>  and `kind`.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.<br>The template dry run succeeded.<br>The response body contains a resource diff of changes that the<br>template would have made if installed.<br>No resources were created or updated.<br>The diff and summary won't contain IDs for resources<br>that didn't exist at the time of the dry run.<br>|[TemplateSummary](#schematemplatesummary)|
|201|Created|Success.<br>The template applied successfully.<br>The response body contains the stack ID, a diff, and a summary.<br>The diff compares the initial state to the state after the template installation.<br>The summary contains newly created resources.<br>|[TemplateSummary](#schematemplatesummary)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity.<br><br><br>The error may indicate one of the following problems:<br><br>- The template failed validation.<br>- You passed a parameter combination that InfluxDB doesn't support.<br>|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Returns this error if creating one of the template<br>  resources (bucket, dashboard, task, user) exceeds your plan’s<br>  adjustable service quotas.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

## Export a new template

<a id="opIdExportTemplate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/templates/export \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "stackID": "string",
    "orgIDs": [
      {
        "orgID": "string",
        "resourceFilters": {
          "byLabel": [
            "string"
          ],
          "byResourceKind": [
            "Bucket"
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "resources": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "kind": "Bucket",
        "name": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-users">Users</h1>

Manage users for your organization.
Users are those with access to InfluxDB.
To grant a user permission to access data, add them as a member of an
organization and provide them with an API token.

### User sessions with authorizations

Optionally, you can scope an authorization (and its API token) to a user.
If a user signs in with username and password, creating a _user session_,
the session carries the permissions granted by all the user's authorizations.
To create a user session, use the [`POST /api/v2/signin` endpoint](#operation/PostSignin).

### Related guides

- [Manage users](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb/latest/users/)
- [Create a token scoped to a user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/latest/security/tokens/create-token/#create-a-token-scoped-to-a-user)

## Update a password

<a id="opIdPutMePassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/me/password \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -H 'Cookie: influxdb-oss-session=influxdb-oss-session=19aaaZZZGOvP2GGryXVT2qYftlFKu3bIopurM6AGFow1yF1abhtOlbHfsc-d8gozZFC_6WxmlQIAwLMW5xs523w==' \
  -d '{
    "password": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /me/password`

Updates the password for the signed-in [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user).

This endpoint represents the third step in the following three-step process to let a
user with a user session update their password:
  1. Pass the user's [Basic authentication credentials](#section/Authentication/BasicAuthentication) to the `POST /api/v2/signin`
     endpoint to create a user session and generate a session cookie.
  2. From the response in the first step, extract the session cookie (`Set-Cookie`) header.
  3. Pass the following in a request to the `PUT /api/v2/me/password` endpoint:
     - The `Set-Cookie` header from the second step
     - The `Authorization Basic` header with the user's _Basic authentication_ credentials
     - `{"password": "NEW_PASSWORD"}` in the request body

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Doesn't let you manage user passwords through the API.
  Use the InfluxDB Cloud user interface (UI) to update your password.

#### Related endpoints

- [Signin](#tag/Signin)
- [Signout](#tag/Signout)
- [Users](#tag/Users)

#### Related guides

- [InfluxDB Cloud - Change your password](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/change-password/)
- [InfluxDB OSS - Change your password](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/users/change-password/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "password": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

|body|body|[PasswordResetBody](#schemapasswordresetbody)|true|The new password.|
|» password|body|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

|400|Bad Request|Bad request.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't let you manage user passwords through the API; always responds with this status.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Doesn't understand a value passed in the request.<br>|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|default|Default|Unsuccessful authentication|[Error](#schemaerror)|

## Create a user

<a id="opIdPostUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "status": "active"
  }'
```

`POST /users`

Creates a [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user) that can access InfluxDB.
Returns the user.

Use this endpoint to create a user that can sign in to start a user session
through one of the following interfaces:

  - InfluxDB UI
  - `/api/v2/signin` InfluxDB API endpoint
  - InfluxDB CLI

This endpoint represents the first two steps in a four-step process to allow a user
to authenticate with a username and password, and then access data in an organization:

  1. Create a user: send a `POST` request to `POST /api/v2/users`. The `name` property is required.
  2. Extract the user ID (`id` property) value from the API response for _step 1_.
  3. Create an authorization (and API token) for the user: send a `POST` request to [`POST /api/v2/authorizations`](#operation/PostAuthorizations), passing the user ID (`id`) from _step 2_.
  4. Create a password for the user: send a `POST` request to [`POST /api/v2/users/USER_ID/password`](#operation/PostUsersIDPassword), passing the user ID from _step 2_.

#### Required permissions

| Action | Permission required | Restriction |
|:-------|:--------------------|:------------|
| Create a user | _[Operator token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/#operator-token)_  | |

#### Related guides

- [Create a user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/users/create-user/)
- [Create an API token scoped to a user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/create-token/#create-a-token-scoped-to-a-user)

```json
}
```

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-security-and-access-endpoints">Security and access endpoints</h1>

## Create a user session.

<a id="opIdPostSignin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/signin \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /signin`

Authenticates [Basic authentication credentials](#section/Authentication/BasicAuthentication)
for a [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user),
and then, if successful, generates a user session.

To authenticate a user, pass the HTTP `Authorization` header with the
`Basic` scheme and the base64-encoded username and password.
For syntax and more information, see [Basic Authentication](#section/Authentication/BasicAuthentication) for
syntax and more information.

If authentication is successful, InfluxDB creates a new session for the user
and then returns the session cookie in the `Set-Cookie` response header.

InfluxDB stores user sessions in memory only.
They expire within ten minutes and during restarts of the InfluxDB instance.

#### User sessions with authorizations

- In InfluxDB Cloud, a user session inherits all the user's permissions for
  the organization.
- In InfluxDB OSS, a user session inherits all the user's permissions for all
  the organizations that the user belongs to.

#### Related endpoints

- [Signout](#tag/Signout)


<h3 id="create-a-user-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-user-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success.<br>The user is authenticated.<br>The `Set-Cookie` response header contains the session cookie.<br>|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized.<br>This error may be caused by one of the following problems:<br><br>- The user doesn't have access.<br>- The user passed incorrect credentials in the request.<br>- The credentials are formatted incorrectly in the request.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden. The user account is disabled.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Unsuccessful authentication.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuthentication
</aside>

## Expire a user session

<a id="opIdPostSignout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/signout \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`POST /signout`

Expires a user session specified by a session cookie.

Use this endpoint to expire a user session that was generated when the user
authenticated with the InfluxDB Developer Console (UI) or the `POST /api/v2/signin` endpoint.

For example, the `POST /api/v2/signout` endpoint represents the third step
in the following three-step process
to authenticate a user, retrieve the `user` resource, and then expire the session:

1. Send a request with the user's [Basic authentication credentials](#section/Authentication/BasicAuthentication)
   to the `POST /api/v2/signin` endpoint to create a user session and
   generate a session cookie.
2. Send a request to the `GET /api/v2/me` endpoint, passing the stored session cookie
   from step 1 to retrieve user information.
3. Send a request to the `POST /api/v2/signout` endpoint, passing the stored session
   cookie to expire the session.

_See the complete example in request samples._

InfluxDB stores user sessions in memory only.
If a user doesn't sign out, then the user session automatically expires within ten minutes or
during a restart of the InfluxDB instance.

To learn more about cookies in HTTP requests, see
[Mozilla Developer Network (MDN) Web Docs, HTTP cookies](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies).

#### Related endpoints

- [Signin](#tag/Signin)

|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

## Update a password

<a id="opIdPutUsersIDPassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/users/string/password \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "password": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{userID}/password`

Updates a user password.

Use this endpoint to let a user authenticate with
[Basic authentication credentials](#section/Authentication/BasicAuthentication)
and set a new password.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Doesn't allow you to manage user passwords through the API.
  Use the InfluxDB Cloud user interface (UI) to update a password.

#### Related guides

- [InfluxDB Cloud - Change your password](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/change-password/)
- [InfluxDB OSS - Change your password](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/users/change-password/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "password": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-password-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|userID|path|string|true|The ID of the user to set the password for.|
|body|body|[PasswordResetBody](#schemapasswordresetbody)|true|The new password to set for the user.|
|» password|body|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "passwords cannot be changed through the InfluxDB Cloud API"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-password-1-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success. The password is updated.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't allow you to manage passwords through the API; always responds with this status.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Doesn't understand a value passed in the request.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuthentication
</aside>

## List users

<a id="opIdGetUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /users`

Lists [users](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user).
Default limit is `20`.

To limit which users are returned, pass query parameters in your request.

#### Required permissions for InfluxDB OSS

| Action | Permission required | Restriction |
|:-------|:--------------------|:------------|
| List all users | _[Operator token](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/security/tokens/#operator-token)_  | |
| List a specific user | `read-users` or `read-user USER_ID` | |

*`USER_ID`* is the ID of the user that you want to retrieve.

#### Related guides

- [View users](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/users/view-users/).


<h3 id="list-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|offset|query|integer|false|The offset for pagination.<br>The number of records to skip.<br><br>For more information about pagination parameters, see [Pagination](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api/#tag/Pagination).<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of records returned. Default is `20`.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A resource ID to seek from.<br>Returns records created after the specified record;<br>results don't include the specified record.<br><br>Use `after` instead of the `offset` parameter.<br>For more information about pagination parameters, see [Pagination](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api/#tag/Pagination).<br>|
|name|query|string|false|A user name.<br>Only lists the specified [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user).<br>|
|id|query|string|false|A user ID.<br>Only lists the specified [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {
    "self": "http://example.com"
  },
  "users": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "status": "active",
      "links": {
        "self": "/api/v2/users/1"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "write:users/09d8462ce0764000 is unauthorized"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="list-users-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success. The response contains a list of `users`.|[Users](#schemausers)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity.<br><br>The error may indicate one of the following problems:<br><br>- The request body isn't valid--the request is well-formed,<br>  but InfluxDB can't process it due to semantic errors.<br>- You passed a parameter combination that InfluxDB doesn't support.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-ping">Ping</h1>

## Get the status of the instance

<a id="opIdGetPing"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/ping \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /ping`

Retrieves the status and InfluxDB version of the instance.

Use this endpoint to monitor uptime for the InfluxDB instance. The response
returns a HTTP `204` status code to inform you the instance is available.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Isn't versioned and doesn't return `X-Influxdb-Version` in the headers.

#### Related guides

- [Influx ping](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/cli/influx/ping/)


<h3 id="get-the-status-of-the-instance-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success.<br>Headers contain InfluxDB version information.<br>|None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|204|X-Influxdb-Build|string||The type of InfluxDB build.<br>|
|204|X-Influxdb-Version|integer||The version of InfluxDB.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br>  - Doesn't return version.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

<a id="opIdGetRoutes"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /`

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-data-io-endpoints">Data I/O endpoints</h1>

## Write data

<a id="opIdPostWrite"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8086/write?org=string&bucket=string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d 'airSensors,sensor_id=TLM0201 temperature=73.97038159354763,humidity=35.23103248356096,co=0.48445310567793615 1630424257000000000
airSensors,sensor_id=TLM0202 temperature=75.30007505999716,humidity=35.651929918691714,co=0.5141876544505826 1630424257000000000
'
```

`POST /write`

Writes data to a bucket.

Use this endpoint to send data in [line protocol](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/line-protocol/) format to InfluxDB.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Does the following when you send a write request:

  1. Validates the request and queues the write.
  2. If queued, responds with _success_ (HTTP `2xx` status code); _error_ otherwise.
  3. Handles the delete asynchronously and reaches eventual consistency.

  To ensure that InfluxDB Cloud handles writes and deletes in the order you request them,
  wait for a success response (HTTP `2xx` status code) before you send the next request.

  Because writes and deletes are asynchronous, your change might not yet be readable
  when you receive the response.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- Validates the request and handles the write synchronously.
- If all points were written successfully, responds with HTTP `2xx` status code;
  otherwise, returns the first line that failed.

#### Required permissions

- `write-buckets` or `write-bucket BUCKET_ID`.

 *`BUCKET_ID`* is the ID of the destination bucket.

#### Rate limits (with InfluxDB Cloud)

`write` rate limits apply.
For more information, see [limits and adjustable quotas](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/limits/).

#### Related guides

- [Write data with the InfluxDB API](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/developer-tools/api)
- [Optimize writes to InfluxDB](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/best-practices/optimize-writes/)
- [Troubleshoot issues writing data](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/troubleshoot/)


> Body parameter

```text
airSensors,sensor_id=TLM0201 temperature=73.97038159354763,humidity=35.23103248356096,co=0.48445310567793615 1630424257000000000
airSensors,sensor_id=TLM0202 temperature=75.30007505999716,humidity=35.651929918691714,co=0.5141876544505826 1630424257000000000

```

<h3 id="write-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|Content-Encoding|header|string|false|The compression applied to the line protocol in the request payload.<br>To send a GZIP payload, pass `Content-Encoding: gzip` header.<br>|
|Content-Type|header|string|false|The format of the data in the request body.<br>To send a line protocol payload, pass `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`.<br>|
|Content-Length|header|integer|false|The size of the entity-body, in bytes, sent to InfluxDB.<br>If the length is greater than the `max body` configuration option,<br>the server responds with status code `413`.<br>|
|Accept|header|string|false|The content type that the client can understand.<br>Writes only return a response body if they fail--for example,<br>due to a formatting problem or quota limit.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>  - Returns only `application/json` for format and limit errors.<br>  - Returns only `text/html` for some quota limit errors.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>  - Returns only `application/json` for format and limit errors.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [Troubleshoot issues writing data](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/troubleshoot/)<br>|
|org|query|string|true|An organization name or ID.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Writes data to the bucket in the organization<br>  associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Requires either the `org` parameter or the `orgID` parameter.<br>- If you pass both `orgID` and `org`, they must both be valid.<br>- Writes data to the bucket in the specified organization.<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Writes data to the bucket in the organization<br>  associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Requires either the `org` parameter or the `orgID` parameter.<br>- If you pass both `orgID` and `org`, they must both be valid.<br>- Writes data to the bucket in the specified organization.<br>|
|bucket|query|string|true|A bucket name or ID.<br>InfluxDB writes all points in the batch to the specified bucket.<br>|
|precision|query|[WritePrecision](#schemawriteprecision)|false|The precision for unix timestamps in the line protocol batch.|
|body|body|string(byte)|true|In the request body, provide data in [line protocol format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/line-protocol/).<br><br>To send compressed data, do the following:<br><br>  1. Use [GZIP](https://www.gzip.org/) to compress the line protocol data.<br>  2. In your request, send the compressed data and the<br>     `Content-Encoding: gzip` header.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [Best practices for optimizing writes](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/best-practices/optimize-writes/)<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|Content-Encoding|gzip|
|Content-Encoding|identity|
|Content-Type|text/plain|
|Content-Type|text/plain; charset=utf-8|
|Accept|application/json|
|precision|ms|
|precision|s|
|precision|us|
|precision|ns|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "partial write error (2 written): unable to parse 'air_sensor,service=S1,sensor=L1 temperature=\"90.5\",humidity=70.0 1632850122': schema: field type for field \"temperature\" not permitted by schema; got String but expected Float"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "not found",
  "message": "organization name \"my-org\" not found"
}
```

> 413 Response

```json
"{\"code\":\"request too large\",\"message\":\"unable to read data: points batch is too large\"}\n"
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="write-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Validated and queued the request.<br>- Handles the write asynchronously - the write might not have completed yet.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Successfully wrote all points in the batch.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [How to check for write errors](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/troubleshoot/)<br>|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request. The response body contains detail about the error.<br><br>InfluxDB returns this error if the line protocol data in the request is malformed.<br>The response body contains the first malformed line in the data, and indicates what was expected.<br>For partial writes, the number of points written and the number of points rejected are also included.<br>For more information, check the `rejected_points` measurement in your `_monitoring` bucket.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Returns this error for bucket schema conflicts.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Returns this error if the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter doesn't match an organization.<br>|[LineProtocolError](#schemalineprotocolerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found.<br>A requested resource was not found.<br>The response body contains the requested resource type and the name value<br>(if you passed it)--for example:<br><br>- `"organization name \"my-org\" not found"`<br>- `"organization not found"`: indicates you passed an ID that did not match<br>   an organization.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|413|Payload Too Large|The request payload is too large.<br>InfluxDB rejected the batch and did not write any data.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud:<br><br> - Returns this error if the payload exceeds the 50MB size limit.<br> - Returns `Content-Type: text/html` for this error.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS:<br><br> - Returns this error only if the [Go (golang) `ioutil.ReadAll()`](https://pkg.go.dev/io/ioutil#ReadAll) function raises an error.<br> - Returns `Content-Type: application/json` for this error.<br>|[LineProtocolLengthError](#schemalineprotocollengtherror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>  - Returns this error if a **read** or **write** request exceeds your plan's [adjustable service quotas](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/limits/#adjustable-service-quotas)<br>    or if a **delete** request exceeds the maximum [global limit](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/limits/#global-limits).<br>  - For rate limits that reset automatically, returns a `Retry-After` header that describes when to try the write again.<br>  - For limits that can't reset (for example, **cardinality limit**), doesn't return a `Retry-After` header.<br><br>  Rates (data-in (writes), queries (reads), and deletes) accrue within a fixed five-minute window.<br>  Once a rate limit is exceeded, InfluxDB returns an error response until the current five-minute window resets.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>  - Doesn't return this error.<br>|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Service unavailable.<br><br>- Returns this error if<br>  the server is temporarily unavailable to accept writes.<br>- Returns a `Retry-After` header that describes when to try the write again.<br>|None|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

|message|string|false|read-only|A human-readable message that may contain detail about the error.|

## Delete data

<a id="opIdPostDelete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/delete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "stop": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "predicate": "tag1=\"value1\" and (tag2=\"value2\" and tag3!=\"value3\")"
  }'
```

`POST /delete`

Deletes data from a bucket.

Use this endpoint to delete points from a bucket in a specified time range.

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- Does the following when you send a delete request:

  1. Validates the request and queues the delete.
  2. If queued, responds with _success_ (HTTP `2xx` status code); _error_ otherwise.
  3. Handles the delete asynchronously and reaches eventual consistency.

To ensure that InfluxDB Cloud handles writes and deletes in the order you request them,
wait for a success response (HTTP `2xx` status code) before you send the next request.

Because writes and deletes are asynchronous, your change might not yet be readable
when you receive the response.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- Validates the request, handles the delete synchronously,
  and then responds with success or failure.

#### Required permissions

- `write-buckets` or `write-bucket BUCKET_ID`.

*`BUCKET_ID`* is the ID of the destination bucket.

#### Rate limits (with InfluxDB Cloud)

`write` rate limits apply.
For more information, see [limits and adjustable quotas](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/limits/).

#### Related guides

- [Delete data](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/delete-data/)
- Learn how to use [delete predicate syntax](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/delete-predicate/).
- Learn how InfluxDB handles [deleted tags](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/stdlib/influxdata/influxdb/schema/measurementtagkeys/)
  and [deleted fields](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/stdlib/influxdata/influxdb/schema/measurementfieldkeys/).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "stop": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "predicate": "tag1=\"value1\" and (tag2=\"value2\" and tag3!=\"value3\")"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|org|query|string|false|An organization name or ID.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Deletes data from the bucket in the organization<br>  associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Requires either the `org` parameter or the `orgID` parameter.<br>- Deletes data from the bucket in the specified organization.<br>- If you pass both `orgID` and `org`, they must both be valid.<br>|
|bucket|query|string|false|A bucket name or ID.<br>Specifies the bucket to delete data from.<br>If you pass both `bucket` and `bucketID`, `bucketID` takes precedence.<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Deletes data from the bucket in the organization<br>  associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Requires either the `org` parameter or the `orgID` parameter.<br>- Deletes data from the bucket in the specified organization.<br>- If you pass both `orgID` and `org`, they must both be valid.<br>|
|bucketID|query|string|false|A bucket ID.<br>Specifies the bucket to delete data from.<br>If you pass both `bucket` and `bucketID`, `bucketID` takes precedence.<br>|
|body|body|[DeletePredicateRequest](#schemadeletepredicaterequest)|true|Time range parameters and an optional **delete predicate expression**.<br><br>To select points to delete within the specified time range, pass a<br>**delete predicate expression** in the `predicate` property of the request body.<br>If you don't pass a `predicate`, InfluxDB deletes all data with timestamps<br>in the specified time range.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [Delete data](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/delete-data/)<br>- Learn how to use [delete predicate syntax](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/delete-predicate/).<br>|
|» start|body|string(date-time)|true|A timestamp ([RFC3339 date/time format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp)).<br>The earliest time to delete from.<br>|
|» stop|body|string(date-time)|true|A timestamp ([RFC3339 date/time format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp)).<br>The latest time to delete from.<br>|
|» predicate|body|string|false|An expression in [delete predicate syntax](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/delete-predicate/).<br>|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid",
  "message": "failed to decode request body: organization not found"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "not found",
  "message": "organization name \"my-org\" not found"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Validated and queued the request.<br>- Handles the delete asynchronously - the deletion might not have completed yet.<br><br>An HTTP `2xx` status code acknowledges that the write or delete is queued.<br>To ensure that InfluxDB Cloud handles writes and deletes in the order you request them,<br>wait for a response before you send the next request.<br><br>Because writes are asynchronous, data might not yet be written<br>when you receive the response.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Deleted the data.<br>|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.<br>The response body contains detail about the error.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Returns this error if the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter doesn't match an organization.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found.<br>A requested resource was not found.<br>The response body contains the requested resource type and the name value<br>(if you passed it)--for example:<br><br>- `"organization name \"my-org\" not found"`<br>- `"organization not found"`: indicates you passed an ID that did not match<br>   an organization.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

`POST /query`

Retrieves data from buckets.

Use this endpoint to send a Flux query request and retrieve data from a bucket.

#### Rate limits (with InfluxDB Cloud)

`read` rate limits apply.
For more information, see [limits and adjustable quotas](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/limits/).

#### Related guides

- [Query with the InfluxDB API](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/query-data/execute-queries/influx-api/)
- [Get started with Flux](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/get-started/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "extern": {
    "type": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "package": {
      "type": "string",
      "name": {
        "type": "string",
        "name": "string"
      }
    },
    "imports": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "as": {
          "type": "string",
          "name": "string"
        },
        "path": {
          "type": "string",
          "value": "string"
        }
      }
    ],
    "body": [
      {
        "type": "string",
        "text": "string"
      }
    ]
  },
  "query": "string",
  "type": "flux",
  "params": {},
  "dialect": {
    "header": true,
    "delimiter": ",",
    "annotations": [
      "group"
    ],
    "commentPrefix": "#",
    "dateTimeFormat": "RFC3339"
  },
  "now": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="query-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|Accept-Encoding|header|string|false|The content encoding (usually a compression algorithm) that the client can understand.|
|Content-Type|header|string|false|none|
|org|query|string|false|An organization name or ID.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Queries the bucket in the organization associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Requires either the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Queries the bucket in the specified organization.<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Doesn't use the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Queries the bucket in the organization associated with the authorization (API token).<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Requires either the `org` parameter or `orgID` parameter.<br>- Queries the bucket in the specified organization.<br>|
|body|body|[Query](#schemaquery)|false|Flux query or specification to execute|
|» extern|body|[File](#schemafile)|false|Represents a source from a single file|
|» query|body|string|true|The query script to execute.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of query. Must be "flux".|
|» params|body|object|false|Key-value pairs passed as parameters during query execution.<br><br>To use parameters in your query, pass a _`query`_ with `params` references (in dot notation)--for example:<br><br>```json<br>  query: "from(bucket: params.mybucket)\<br>              \|> range(start: params.rangeStart) \|> limit(n:1)"<br>```<br><br>and pass _`params`_ with the key-value pairs--for example:<br><br>```json<br>  params: {<br>    "mybucket": "environment",<br>    "rangeStart": "-30d"<br>  }<br>```<br><br>During query execution, InfluxDB passes _`params`_ to your script and substitutes the values.<br><br>#### Limitations<br><br>- If you use _`params`_, you can't use _`extern`_.<br>|
|» dialect|body|[Dialect](#schemadialect)|false|Options for tabular data output.<br>Default output is [annotated CSV](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/annotated-csv/#csv-response-format) with headers.<br><br>For more information about tabular data **dialect**,<br>see [W3 metadata vocabulary for tabular data](https://www.w3.org/TR/2015/REC-tabular-metadata-20151217/#dialect-descriptions).<br>|
|» now|body|string(date-time)|false|Specifies the time that should be reported as `now` in the query.<br>Default is the server `now` time.<br>|

## Start a task run, overriding the schedule

<a id="opIdPostTasksIDRuns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks/string/runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "scheduledFor": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /tasks/{taskID}/runs`

Schedules a task run to start immediately, ignoring scheduled runs.

Use this endpoint to manually start a task run.
Scheduled runs will continue to run as scheduled.
This may result in concurrently running tasks.

To _retry_ a previous run (and avoid creating a new run),
use the [`POST /api/v2/tasks/{taskID}/runs/{runID}/retry` endpoint](#operation/PostTasksIDRunsIDRetry).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "scheduledFor": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|taskID|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[RunManually](#schemarunmanually)|false|none|
|» scheduledFor|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The time [RFC3339 date/time format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp)<br>used for the run's `now` option.<br>Default is the server _now_ time.<br>|

```json
    {
      "time": "2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00",
      "message": "Halt and catch fire",
      "runID": "string"
    }
  ],

  }
}
```

## List tasks

<a id="opIdGetTasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /tasks`

Retrieves a list of [tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task).

To limit which tasks are returned, pass query parameters in your request.
If no query parameters are passed, InfluxDB returns all tasks up to the default `limit`.

#### Related guide

- [Process data with InfluxDB tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/)


<h3 id="list-tasks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|name|query|string|false|A [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task) name.<br>Only returns tasks with the specified name.<br>Different tasks may have the same name.<br>|
|after|query|string|false|A [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task) ID.<br>Only returns tasks created after the specified task.<br>|
|user|query|string|false|A [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user) ID.<br>Only returns tasks owned by the specified user.<br>|
|org|query|string|false|An [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization) name.<br>Only returns tasks owned by the specified organization.<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization) ID.<br>Only returns tasks owned by the specified organization.<br>|
|status|query|string|false|A [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task) status.<br>Only returns tasks that have the specified status (`active` or `inactive`).<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of [tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task) to return.<br>Default is `100`.<br>The minimum is `1` and the maximum is `500`.<br><br>To reduce the payload size, combine _`type=basic`_ and _`limit`_ (see _Request samples_).<br>For more information about the `basic` response, see the _`type`_ parameter.<br>|
|type|query|string|false|A [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task) type (`basic` or `system`).<br>Default is `system`.<br>Specifies the level of detail for tasks in the response.<br>The default (`system`) response contains all the metadata properties for tasks.<br>To reduce the response size, pass `basic` to omit some task properties (`flux`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|inactive|
|type|basic|
|type|system|

## Create a task

<a id="opIdPostTasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "orgID": "string",
    "org": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "flux": "string",
    "description": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /tasks`

Creates a [task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#task)  and returns the task.

#### Related guides

- [Get started with tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/get-started/)
- [Create a task](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/manage-tasks/create-task/)
- [Common tasks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/common-tasks/)
- [Task configuration options](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/process-data/task-options/)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "orgID": "string",
  "org": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "flux": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|body|body|[TaskCreateRequest](#schemataskcreaterequest)|true|The task to create.|
|» orgID|body|string|false|The ID of the organization that owns this Task.|
|» org|body|string|false|The name of the organization that owns this Task.|
|» status|body|[TaskStatusType](#schemataskstatustype)|false|`inactive` cancels scheduled runs and prevents manual runs of the task.<br>|
|» flux|body|string|true|The Flux script to run for this task.|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional description of the task.|

|404|Not Found|Not found.<br>A requested resource was not found.<br>The response body contains the requested resource type and the name value<br>(if you passed it)--for example:<br><br>- `"organization name \"my-org\" not found"`<br>- `"organization not found"`: indicates you passed an ID that did not match<br>   an organization.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

|---|---|

## List dashboards

<a id="opIdGetDashboards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/dashboards \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /dashboards`

Lists [dashboards](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#dashboard).

#### Related guides

- [Manage dashboards](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/visualize-data/dashboards/).


<h3 id="list-dashboards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|
|offset|query|integer|false|The offset for pagination.<br>The number of records to skip.<br><br>For more information about pagination parameters, see [Pagination](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/api/#tag/Pagination).<br>|
|limit|query|integer|false|Limits the number of records returned. Default is `20`.<br>|
|descending|query|boolean|false|none|
|owner|query|string|false|A user ID. Only returns [dashboards](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#dashboard) where the specified user has the `owner` role.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The column to sort by.|
|id|query|[string]|false|A list of dashboard IDs.<br>Returns only the specified [dashboards](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#dashboard).<br>If you specify `id` and `owner`, only `id` is used.<br>|
|orgID|query|string|false|An organization ID.<br>Only returns [dashboards](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#dashboard) that belong to the specified<br>[organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization).<br>|
|org|query|string|false|An organization name.<br>Only returns [dashboards](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#dashboard) that belong to the specified<br>[organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sortBy|ID|
|sortBy|CreatedAt|
|sortBy|UpdatedAt|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {
    "next": "http://example.com",
    "self": "http://example.com",
    "prev": "http://example.com"
  },
  "dashboards": [
    {
      "orgID": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "links": {
        "self": "/api/v2/dashboards/1",
        "cells": "/api/v2/dashboards/1/cells",
        "owners": "/api/v2/dashboards/1/owners",
        "members": "/api/v2/dashboards/1/members",
        "labels": "/api/v2/dashboards/1/labels",
        "org": "/api/v2/labels/1"
      },
      "id": "string",
      "meta": {
        "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      },
      "cells": [
        {
          "id": "string",
          "links": {
            "self": "string",
            "view": "string"
          },
          "x": 0,
          "y": 0,
          "w": 0,
          "h": 0,
          "viewID": "string"
        }
      ],
      "labels": [
        {
          "id": "string",
          "orgID": "string",
          "name": "string",
          "properties": {
            "color": "ffb3b3",
            "description": "this is a description"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|default|Default|Unexpected error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

TokenAuthentication

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-config">Config</h1>

## Retrieve feature flags

<a id="opIdGetFlags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/flags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /flags`

Retrieves the feature flag key-value pairs configured for the InfluxDB
instance.
_Feature flags_ are configuration options used to develop and test
experimental InfluxDB features and are intended for internal use only.

This endpoint represents the first step in the following three-step process
to configure feature flags:

1. Use [token authentication](#section/Authentication/TokenAuthentication) or a [user session](#tag/Signin) with this endpoint to retrieve
   feature flags and their values.
2. Follow the instructions to [enable, disable, or override values for feature flags](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/config-options/#feature-flags).
3. **Optional**: To confirm that your change is applied, do one of the following:

   - Send a request to this endpoint to retrieve the current feature flag values.
   - Send a request to the [`GET /api/v2/config` endpoint](#operation/GetConfig) to retrieve the
     current runtime server configuration.

#### Related guides

- [InfluxDB configuration options](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/config-options/)


<h3 id="retrieve-feature-flags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unauthorized",
  "message": "unauthorized access"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-feature-flags-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success. The response body contains feature flags.|[Flags](#schemaflags)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. The error may indicate one of the following:<br><br>  * The `Authorization: Token` header is missing or malformed.<br>  * The API token value is missing from the header.<br>  * The token doesn't have sufficient permissions to write to this organization and bucket.<br>|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.<br>The server encountered an unexpected situation.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="retrieve-feature-flags-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **401**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|read-only|The HTTP status code description. Default is `unauthorized`.<br>|
|message|string|false|read-only|A human-readable message that may contain detail about the error.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|unauthorized|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

`GET /config`

Returns the active runtime configuration of the InfluxDB instance.

In InfluxDB v2.2+, use this endpoint to view your active runtime configuration,
including flags and environment variables.

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-health">Health</h1>

## Retrieve the health of the instance

<a id="opIdGetHealth"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/health \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /health`

Returns the health of the instance.

`--health-auth-mode` and `--hardening-enabled` reduce the response body
for callers without operator permissions.
Those callers don't receive check messages, measure groups, `version`,
or `commit`.
The status code never changes.


<h3 id="retrieve-the-health-of-the-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "name": "influxdb",
  "status": "pass",
  "message": "healthy",
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "shards",
      "status": "pass",
      "failures": {
        "count": 0,
        "unit": "shards"
      }
    }
  ],
  "version": "v2.10.0",
  "commit": "310ee146d9"
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "checks": [
    {}
  ],
  "status": "pass",
  "version": "string",
  "commit": "string",
  "property1": {
    "completed": 94,
    "total": 200,
    "unit": "shards"
  },
  "property2": {
    "completed": 94,
    "total": 200,
    "unit": "shards"
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-the-health-of-the-instance-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The instance is healthy.<br>The response body contains the health check items and status.<br>|[HealthCheck](#schemahealthcheck)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The instance is unhealthy.<br>`message` contains the message of the first failing check.<br>|[HealthCheck](#schemahealthcheck)|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

<h1 id="influxdb-oss-api-service-metrics">Metrics</h1>

## Retrieve workload performance metrics

<a id="opIdGetMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8086/metrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /metrics`

Returns metrics about the workload performance of an InfluxDB instance.

Use this endpoint to get performance, resource, and usage metrics.

#### Related guides

- For the list of metrics categories, see [InfluxDB OSS metrics](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/internals/metrics/).
- Learn how to use InfluxDB to [scrape Prometheus metrics](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/write-data/developer-tools/scrape-prometheus-metrics/).
- Learn how InfluxDB [parses the Prometheus exposition format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/prometheus-metrics/).


<h3 id="retrieve-workload-performance-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zap-Trace-Span|header|string|false|OpenTracing span context|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
# HELP go_threads Number of OS threads created.
# TYPE go_threads gauge
go_threads 19
# HELP http_api_request_duration_seconds Time taken to respond to HTTP request
# TYPE http_api_request_duration_seconds histogram
http_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{handler="platform",method="GET",path="/:fallback_path",response_code="200",status="2XX",user_agent="curl",le="0.005"} 4
http_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{handler="platform",method="GET",path="/:fallback_path",response_code="200",status="2XX",user_agent="curl",le="0.01"} 4
http_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{handler="platform",method="GET",path="/:fallback_path",response_code="200",status="2XX",user_agent="curl",le="0.025"} 5

```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "internal error",
  "message": "string",
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-workload-performance-metrics-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success. The response body contains metrics in<br>[Prometheus plain-text exposition format](https://prometheus.io/docs/instrumenting/exposition_formats)<br>Metrics contain a name, an optional set of key-value pairs, and a value.<br><br>The following descriptors precede each metric:<br><br>- `HELP`: description of the metric<br>- `TYPE`: [Prometheus metric type](https://prometheus.io/docs/concepts/metric_types/) (`counter`, `gauge`, `histogram`, or `summary`)<br>|Inline|
|default|Default|Non 2XX error response from server.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
TokenAuthentication
</aside>

```json
  "status": "ready",

  }
```

```json
{
  "status": "starting",
  "started": "2026-05-26T15:42:30.123456789Z",
  "up": "1.2s",
  "uptime": {
    "value": 1.2,
    "unit": "seconds"
  },
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "shards",

      }

```

```json
  "op": "string",
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h2 id="tocS_LanguageRequest">LanguageRequest</h2>

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|params|object|false|none|Key-value pairs passed as parameters during query execution.<br><br>To use parameters in your query, pass a _`query`_ with `params` references (in dot notation)--for example:<br><br>```json<br>  query: "from(bucket: params.mybucket)\<br>              \|> range(start: params.rangeStart) \|> limit(n:1)"<br>```<br><br>and pass _`params`_ with the key-value pairs--for example:<br><br>```json<br>  params: {<br>    "mybucket": "environment",<br>    "rangeStart": "-30d"<br>  }<br>```<br><br>During query execution, InfluxDB passes _`params`_ to your script and substitutes the values.<br><br>#### Limitations<br><br>- If you use _`params`_, you can't use _`extern`_.<br>|
|dialect|[Dialect](#schemadialect)|false|none|Options for tabular data output.<br>Default output is [annotated CSV](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/annotated-csv/#csv-response-format) with headers.<br><br>For more information about tabular data **dialect**,<br>see [W3 metadata vocabulary for tabular data](https://www.w3.org/TR/2015/REC-tabular-metadata-20151217/#dialect-descriptions).<br>|
|now|string(date-time)|false|none|Specifies the time that should be reported as `now` in the query.<br>Default is the server `now` time.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Dialect">Dialect</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadialect"></a>
<a id="schema_Dialect"></a>
<a id="tocSdialect"></a>
<a id="tocsdialect"></a>

```json
{
  "header": true,
  "delimiter": ",",
  "annotations": [
    "group"
  ],
  "commentPrefix": "#",
  "dateTimeFormat": "RFC3339"
}
```

Options for tabular data output.
Default output is [annotated CSV](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/annotated-csv/#csv-response-format) with headers.

For more information about tabular data **dialect**,
see [W3 metadata vocabulary for tabular data](https://www.w3.org/TR/2015/REC-tabular-metadata-20151217/#dialect-descriptions).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|header|boolean|false|none|If true, the results contain a header row.|
|delimiter|string|false|none|The separator used between cells. Default is a comma (`,`).|
|annotations|[string]|false|none|Annotation rows to include in the results.<br>An _annotation_ is metadata associated with an object (column) in the data model.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- See [Annotated CSV annotations](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/syntax/annotated-csv/#annotations) for examples and more information.<br><br>For more information about **annotations** in tabular data,<br>see [W3 metadata vocabulary for tabular data](https://www.w3.org/TR/2015/REC-tabular-data-model-20151217/#columns).<br>|
|commentPrefix|string|false|none|The character prefixed to comment strings. Default is a number sign (`#`).|
|dateTimeFormat|string|false|none|The format for timestamps in results.<br>Default is [`RFC3339` date/time format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp).<br>To include nanoseconds in timestamps, use `RFC3339Nano`.<br><br>#### Example formatted date/time values<br><br>\| Format      \| Value                       \|<br>\|:------------\|:----------------------------\|<br>\| `RFC3339`    \| `"2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00"` \|<br>\| `RFC3339Nano` \| `"2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00"` \|<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|annotations|group|
|annotations|datatype|
|annotations|default|
|dateTimeFormat|RFC3339|
|dateTimeFormat|RFC3339Nano|

<h2 id="tocS_Authorization">Authorization</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

```json
{
  "status": "active",
  "description": "string",
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "orgID": "string",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "action": "read",
      "resource": {
        "type": "authorizations",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "orgID": "string",
        "org": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "id": "string",
  "token": "string",
  "userID": "string",
  "user": "string",
  "org": "string",
  "links": {
    "self": "/api/v2/authorizations/1",
    "user": "/api/v2/users/12"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|string|false|none|Status of the token. If `inactive`, InfluxDB rejects requests that use the token.|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the token.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|none|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|none|
|orgID|string|true|none|The organization ID.<br>Specifies the [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization) that the authorization is scoped to.<br>|
|permissions|[[Permission](#schemapermission)]|true|none|The list of permissions.<br>An authorization must have at least one permission.<br>|
|id|string|false|read-only|The authorization ID.|
|token|string|false|read-only|The API token.<br>The token value is unique to the authorization.<br>[API tokens](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#token) are<br>used to authenticate and authorize InfluxDB API requests and `influx`<br>CLI commands--after receiving the request, InfluxDB checks that the<br>token is valid and that the `permissions` allow the requested action(s).<br>|
|userID|string|false|read-only|The user ID. Specifies the [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user) that owns the authorization. If _scoped_, the user that the authorization is scoped to; otherwise, the creator of the authorization.|
|user|string|false|read-only|The user name.<br>Specifies the [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user) that owns the authorization.<br>If the authorization is _scoped_ to a user, the user;<br>otherwise, the creator of the authorization.<br>|
|org|string|false|read-only|The organization name.<br>Specifies the [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization)<br>that the token is scoped to.<br>|
|links|object|false|read-only|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|inactive|
