|retentionRules|[RetentionRules](#schemaretentionrules)|false|none|Retention rules to expire or retain data.<br>The InfluxDB `/api/v2` API uses `RetentionRules` to configure the [retention period](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#retention-period).<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- `retentionRules` is required.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- `retentionRules` isn't required.<br>|
|schemaType|[SchemaType](#schemaschematype)|false|none|The schema Type. Default is `implicit`.<br><br>#### InfluxDB Cloud<br><br>- Use `explicit` to enforce column names, tags, fields, and data types for<br>your data.<br><br>#### InfluxDB OSS<br><br>- Doesn't support `explicit` bucket schemas.<br>|

Retention rules to expire or retain data.
The InfluxDB `/api/v2` API uses `RetentionRules` to configure the [retention period](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#retention-period).

#### InfluxDB Cloud

- `retentionRules` is required.

#### InfluxDB OSS

- `retentionRules` isn't required.

```json
{
  "dryRun": true,
  "orgID": "string",
  "stackID": "string",

    "contentType": "string",
    "sources": [
      "string"
    ],
    "contents": [
      {
        "apiVersion": "influxdata.com/v2alpha1",
        "kind": "Bucket",
        "metadata": {
          "name": "string"
        },
        "spec": {}
      }
    ]
  },
  "templates": [
    {
      "contentType": "string",
      "sources": [
        "string"
      ],
      "contents": [
        {
          "apiVersion": "influxdata.com/v2alpha1",
          "kind": "Bucket",
          "metadata": {
            "name": "string"
          },
          "spec": {}
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "envRefs": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "secrets": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "remotes": [
    {
      "url": "string",
      "contentType": "string"
    }
  ],
  "actions": [
    {
      "action": "skipKind",
      "properties": {
        "kind": "Bucket"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dryRun|boolean|false|none|Only applies a dry run of the templates passed in the request.<br><br>- Validates the template and generates a resource diff and summary.<br>- Doesn't install templates or make changes to the InfluxDB instance.<br>|
|orgID|string|false|none|Organization ID.<br>InfluxDB applies templates to this organization.<br>The organization owns all resources created by the template.<br><br>To find your organization, see how to<br>[view organizations](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/organizations/view-orgs/).<br>|
|stackID|string|false|none|ID of the stack to update.<br><br>To apply templates to an existing stack in the organization, use the `stackID` parameter.<br>If you apply templates without providing a stack ID,<br>InfluxDB initializes a new stack with all new resources.<br><br>To find a stack ID, use the InfluxDB [`/api/v2/stacks` API endpoint](#operation/ListStacks) to list stacks.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [Stacks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/)<br>- [View stacks](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/stacks/view/)<br>|
|template|object|false|none|A template object to apply.<br>A template object has a `contents` property<br>with an array of InfluxDB resource configurations.<br><br>Pass `template` to apply only one template object.<br>If you use `template`, you can't use the `templates` parameter.<br>If you want to apply multiple template objects, use `templates` instead.<br>|
|templates|[object]|false|none|A list of template objects to apply.<br>A template object has a `contents` property<br>with an array of InfluxDB resource configurations.<br><br>Use the `templates` parameter to apply multiple template objects.<br>If you use `templates`, you can't use the `template` parameter.<br>|
|envRefs|object|false|none|An object with key-value pairs that map to **environment references** in templates.<br><br>Environment references in templates are `envRef` objects with an `envRef.key`<br>property.<br>To substitute a custom environment reference value when applying templates,<br>pass `envRefs` with the `envRef.key` and the value.<br><br>When you apply a template, InfluxDB replaces `envRef` objects in the template<br>with the values that you provide in the `envRefs` parameter.<br>For more examples, see how to [define environment references](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/#define-environment-references).<br><br>The following template fields may use environment references:<br><br>  - `metadata.name`<br>  - `spec.endpointName`<br>  - `spec.associations.name`<br><br>For more information about including environment references in template fields, see how to<br>[include user-definable resource names](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/create/#include-user-definable-resource-names).<br>|
|secrets|object|false|none|An object with key-value pairs that map to **secrets** in queries.<br><br>Queries may reference secrets stored in InfluxDB--for example,<br>the following Flux script retrieves `POSTGRES_USERNAME` and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`<br>secrets and then uses them to connect to a PostgreSQL database:<br><br>```js<br>import "sql"<br>import "influxdata/influxdb/secrets"<br><br>username = secrets.get(key: "POSTGRES_USERNAME")<br>password = secrets.get(key: "POSTGRES_PASSWORD")<br><br>sql.from(<br>  driverName: "postgres",<br>  dataSourceName: "postgresql://${username}:${password}@localhost:5432",<br>  query: "SELECT * FROM example_table",<br>)<br>```<br><br>To define secret values in your `/api/v2/templates/apply` request,<br>pass the `secrets` parameter with key-value pairs--for example:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>  ...<br>  "secrets": {<br>    "POSTGRES_USERNAME": "pguser",<br>    "POSTGRES_PASSWORD": "foo"<br>  }<br>  ...<br>}<br>```<br><br>InfluxDB stores the key-value pairs as secrets that you can access with `secrets.get()`.<br>Once stored, you can't view secret values in InfluxDB.<br><br>#### Related guides<br><br>- [How to pass secrets when installing a template](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/influxdb-templates/use/#pass-secrets-when-installing-a-template)<br>|
|remotes|[object]|false|none|A list of URLs for template files.<br><br>To apply a template manifest file located at a URL, pass `remotes`<br>with an array that contains the URL.<br>|
|actions|[object]|false|none|A list of `action` objects.<br>Actions let you customize how InfluxDB applies templates in the request.<br><br>You can use the following actions to prevent creating or updating resources:<br><br>- A `skipKind` action skips template resources of a specified `kind`.<br>- A `skipResource` action skips template resources with a specified `metadata.name`<br>  and `kind`.<br>|

```json
    "unit": "shards"
  },
  "property2": {
    "completed": 94,
    "total": 200,
    "unit": "shards"
  }
}
```

A health check.
A check can also report measure groups, such as `progress` or `failures`.
Each key other than `name`, `status`, `message`, and `checks` whose value
is an object is a measure group.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|none|
|message|string|false|none|Status detail. For a failing check, may contain the raw error text.<br>|
|checks|[[HealthCheck](#schemahealthcheck)]|false|none|none|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|version|string|false|none|Build version. Returned only at the top level.|
|commit|string|false|none|Build commit. Returned only at the top level.|
|**additionalProperties**|[HealthCheckMeasure](#schemahealthcheckmeasure)|false|none|A measure group: one or more numeric values that share a unit.<br>Durations are float seconds with `unit: seconds`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pass|
|status|fail|

|retention_policy|string|true|none|A [retention policy](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1.8/concepts/glossary/#retention-policy-rp) name.<br>Identifies the InfluxDB v1 retention policy mapping.<br>|

```json
    "runs": "/api/v2/tasks/1/runs",
    "logs": "/api/v2/tasks/1/logs"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|read-only|none|
|orgID|string|true|none|An [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization) ID.<br>Specifies the organization that owns the task.<br>|
|org|string|false|none|An [organization](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#organization) name.<br>Specifies the organization that owns the task.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the task.|
|ownerID|string|false|none|A [user](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#user) ID.<br>Specifies the owner of the task.<br><br>To find a user ID, you can use the<br>[`GET /api/v2/users` endpoint](#operation/GetUsers) to<br>list users.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|A description of the task.|
|status|[TaskStatusType](#schemataskstatustype)|false|none|`inactive` cancels scheduled runs and prevents manual runs of the task.<br>|
|labels|[Labels](#schemalabels)|false|none|none|
|authorizationID|string|false|none|An authorization ID.<br>Specifies the authorization used when the task communicates with the query engine.<br><br>To find an authorization ID, use the<br>[`GET /api/v2/authorizations` endpoint](#operation/GetAuthorizations) to<br>list authorizations.<br>|
|flux|string(flux)|true|none|The Flux script that the task executes.|
|every|string(duration)|false|none|The interval ([duration literal](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp)) at which the task runs. `every` also determines when the task first runs, depending on the specified time.|
|cron|string|false|none|A [Cron expression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cron#Overview) that defines the schedule on which the task runs. InfluxDB uses the system time when evaluating Cron expressions.|
|offset|string(duration)|false|none|A [duration](https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0.x/spec/lexical-elements/#duration-literals) to delay execution of the task after the scheduled time has elapsed. `0` removes the offset.|
|latestCompleted|string(date-time)|false|read-only|A timestamp ([RFC3339 date/time format](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/latest/reference/glossary/#rfc3339-timestamp)) of the latest scheduled and completed run.|
|lastRunStatus|string|false|read-only|none|
|lastRunError|string|false|read-only|none|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|none|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|none|
|links|object|false|read-only|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|inactive|
|lastRunStatus|failed|
|lastRunStatus|success|
|lastRunStatus|canceled|
